jsc.guide.files_and_file_handles.problem: The program stops and says that the file was not found.
The program stops and says that the file was opened with "r", which does not write.
The program stops and says that the file was opened with "w", which does not read.
The program stops and says that the file is closed.
Write or Append gives false, and the file's message says there is not enough free space on the disk.
Write gives false, and the message says the file is read-only.
Write gives false, and the message says the file name is not valid for this filesystem.
Delete gives false for a .dat file.
Move gives false, and the message says a file of that name is already there.
Move gives false: a file on another machine is copied, not moved.
MkDir gives false: the drive has no folders.
jsc.guide.files_and_file_handles.table1_: Renames the file. False when refused. Version 2.
Yes when the file can be read.
The whole text of the file. Stops the program when the file is missing.
True and the text when the file is read. False and empty text otherwise.
Replaces the file with the text. False when the write did not happen.
Adds the text to the end of the file. False when the add did not happen.
Removes the file. False when refused.
Makes a folder. False when refused.
The names in a folder, as a list.
Opens a file to work on it piece by piece: gives a FILE, or null. Version 2.
jsc.guide.files_and_file_handles.table2_: Writes the text to the disk, if it changed, and closes the file.
Gives the next line. False at the end, with an empty line.
The next character as a number, or -1 at the end.
Reads one value of the variable's type.
Writes the text into the file.
Moves to a place, counted in characters from the start and kept between 0 and the length of the file.
The place now, in characters from the start.
Yes when the place is at the end of the file.
jsc.guide.files_and_file_handles.table3_: Reads a file that exists. Gives null when it is missing.
Writes a file, and starts it empty.
Adds text at the end of the file.
Reads and writes a file that exists.
Writes a file that starts empty, and reads it too.
Adds at the end, and reads too.
jsc.guide.files_and_file_handles.text1: A file is a named piece of data on a disk. Its path is its full name: the drive letter that names the disk, then the folders, then the file's own name.
jsc.guide.files_and_file_handles.text2: There are two ways to work on a file. File works on a whole file at once: it reads all of it, or writes all of it. File.Open gives you a FILE instead, which you read and write a piece at a time until you close it.
jsc.guide.files_and_file_handles.text3: Exists, Read and TryRead only look at a file. Write, Append, Delete, MkDir and Move change the disk, and each of them answers true when the change happened.
jsc.guide.files_and_file_handles.text4: File.Read stops the program when the file is missing or cannot be read. The console then shows the file's message, such as "<path>: file not found". Use File.TryRead when you want to ask first and carry on either way.
jsc.guide.files_and_file_handles.text5: A FILE is a file the program has opened. It came in version 2, and all its members are version 2 too. The program works on its own copy of the text, and nothing reaches the disk until you call Close, or until the program ends with the file still open.
jsc.guide.files_and_file_handles.text6: The mode says how a file is opened. The letters b and t are ignored, so rb means r.
jsc.guide.files_and_file_handles.title: Files: whole files and files you open
jsc.guide.files_and_file_handles.warning: Opening a file with w starts it empty, so the text it held is replaced by what the program writes.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.definitio: The Linux file system that the root filesystem uses. The program mke2fs makes it.
The simple file system that the firmware reads from the EFI system partition. It is also called FAT32 or vfat.
The unit that ext4 stores data in: 4 KiB, which is 4,096 bytes.
One record for each file or folder, which says what it is and where its data is. Its number is fixed when the file system is made.
The header of a file system, with its size and layout. Backups are spare copies of it.
A small area where ext4 writes each change before it makes the change final, so that a crash does not damage the file system.
A universally unique identifier, a long number that names one file system. The new system's file table, /etc/fstab, can name a file system by its UUID, so the device name of the disk does not matter.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.fix1: You did not name a partition. Type mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda2, with the name lsblk gave it.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.fix2: That partition does not exist yet. Make it with fdisk first, or check its number in lsblk.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.fix3: That partition holds the boot loader, so it is not for ext4. Format it with mkfs.fat -F 32 /dev/sda1, and give mkfs.ext4 the other partition.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.fix4: You named the whole disk, and it has a partition table. Use one of its partitions, such as /dev/sda2.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.fix5: You did not name a partition. Type mkfs.fat -F 32 /dev/sda1, with the name lsblk gave it.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.fix6: That partition does not exist. Make it with fdisk first, or check its number in lsblk.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.fix7: Set its type first: fdisk /dev/sda, then type t, then type 1 for EFI System, then type w. Then run mkfs.fat again.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.problem2: mke2fs: No such file or directory while trying to determine filesystem size
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.problem3: mke2fs: sda1 is the EFI System partition.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.problem6: mkfs.fat: unable to open sda1: No such file or directory
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.problem7: mkfs.fat: sda1 is not an EFI System partition.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.table1_1_: The version of mke2fs, the program behind mkfs.ext4 that makes ext4.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.table1_2_: How many blocks of 4 kibibytes (KiB) and how many inodes the file system has, which depend on its size.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.table1_3_: The identifier of this file system, a universally unique identifier (UUID), the same every time for that disk.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.table1_4_: Printed only for a file system bigger than 128 megabytes (MB): the numbers of the blocks that hold spare copies of its header.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.table1_5_: A counting bar, which ends with done.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.table1_6_: A counting bar, which ends with done.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.table1_7_: Printed when the file system has a journal, and then done.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.table1_8_: The last step, a counting bar, which ends with done.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.text1: A partition is an empty space until it holds a file system, which decides how its files are stored. The new system's root goes on an ext4 file system (the fourth extended file system), and the EFI system partition gets a FAT (File Allocation Table) file system.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.text2: Each command below makes one file system, and it erases what was on the partition before. Make a file system only on the partition you have divided for it.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.text3: ext4 is the file system the Linux systems keep their root on. The command mkfs.ext4 makes it, with the name of the partition after it: mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda2.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.text4: The partition you name becomes the root. There is only one root at a time: a second mkfs.ext4 on another partition makes that one the root instead. A root that was mounted is unmounted by the new format.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.text5: Making the file system takes time, which depends on the disk. A hard disk takes 140 ticks, which is 7 seconds. A solid-state drive (SSD) takes 35 ticks, and an NVMe (non-volatile memory express) disk takes 24 ticks, the least it can take. 20 ticks make one second ([](jsc:units_and_ticks)).
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.text6: The tool prints these lines as it works, in this order:
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.text7: On a whole disk that has no partition table, the command also works. This is the way of the older machines, which start from the whole disk and have no EFI system partition ([](jsc:eras)).
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.text8: Type mkfs.fat -F 32 /dev/sda1, with the name of the EFI system partition. The tool does not check the -F 32, so type it anyway, as shown.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.text9: The tool waits a short while, then prints one line and nothing else: "mkfs.fat 4.2 (2021-01-31)". It takes 17 ticks on a hard disk and 8 ticks on an SSD or NVMe disk. The partition is formatted and not mounted, so you mount it yourself later.
jsc.guide.filesystems_and_mkfs.title: Giving a partition a file system
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.definition1: The systems and the parts of a machine that a command needs before the machine offers it.
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.fix1: The server has listcmd off. Type help instead to list the commands.
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.fix2: This machine lacks something the command needs, such as a disk, a network or a port for peripherals. Or the command belongs to a package you have not installed yet.
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.fix3: The word is not a command on this machine, and no program of that name is installed. Check the spelling, or type help to list the commands.
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.fix4: Install that package first ([](jsc:software_verbs)). Then the command is on the machine.
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.problem2: A command is missing from help.
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.problem3: The shell says command not found: NAME
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.problem4: The page says it works once a package is installed.
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.table1_1_2: The commands this machine has, one line each. MC-DOS and MC-NET show them on the whole screen; Frames prints them.
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.table1_3_2: Every command and every program on this machine, in one list.
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.text1: Every command has a page of its own, and the page is the same text that help and the switch /? print. You can list the commands the machine has, or ask for the page of one command you already know. Type the first letters of a name and press [[Tab]] to finish it.
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.text2: Each command has a scope. A command works only on the systems it names, and only on a machine with the parts it needs, such as a disk for the file commands or a network for iql. When a part is missing, the command is not in help, and typing it gives a message.
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.text3: listcmd lists everything this machine can run: the commands it offers and every program installed on it, in one list. Its list has a COMMANDS heading with one line per command, then a PROGRAMS heading with each program's name and id. It is off unless the server's settings turn it on.
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.text4: On Linux and the other Unix systems, man opens the page of a Unix command. Those commands are explained in the Unix books, in [finding help](jsc:man_pages).
jsc.guide.finding_a_command.title: Finding a command
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.definiti: A word typed at the prompt that makes the system do one job, such as ls, help or man.
The short written page that explains one command: its name, its form, what it does and its options.
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.fix1: info is on Linux only. On UNIX System V and FreeBSD, use man <command>; on MC-DOS, MC-NET and Frames, use help <command>.
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.fix2: The server has the switch off. Read the listcmd page ([](jsc:listcmd)) to see how it is turned on.
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.problem1: The reply is "command not found: info", or on FreeBSD "info: not found. Try: apropos <word>, or man intro".
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.problem2: The reply is "command not found: listcmd".
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.table1_1: MC-DOS, MC-NET, Frames, Linux, UNIX System V
A command list, or one command's page; full screen on MC-DOS and MC-NET.
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.table1_2: A command's manual page, and the entries of the manuals.
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.table1_3: One line that says what a command is for.
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.table1_4: The commands whose name or summary holds a word you give.
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.table1_5: The manuals as linked screens, read with keys.
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.table1_6: Every system, when the server allows it
Every command and program this computer has.
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.table2_1: How a command is used, when you know its name
help <command> where help exists; man <command> on UNIX systems
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.table2_2: What a command is for, in one line
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.table2_3: A command, found by what it does
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.table2_4: Every manual and command, read as linked screens
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.table2_5: Every command and program this computer has
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.text1: Forgot the name of a command, or the option you need? You can ask the computer at the prompt, without leaving the terminal. Five tools answer the question what a command does, and one tool lists every command the computer has.
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.text2: Each tool works on some systems and not on others. The same pages appear in every book that holds these chapters, so each page says which systems it applies to.
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.text3: Most systems answer an unknown word with "command not found:" and the word, then a hint to type help. UNIX System V answers with the word and "not found" only, and FreeBSD, which has no help command, points you to apropos and man intro.
jsc.guide.finding_help_overview.title: Where to look
jsc.guide.firmware.definition1: The order the firmware tries the disks in when the computer starts. The first disk with a system on it starts.
jsc.guide.firmware.definition2: Basic Input/Output System: the older kind of firmware. The Vintage, Legacy and Transition boards have a BIOS.
jsc.guide.firmware.definition3: Unified Extensible Firmware Interface: the newer kind of firmware. The Standard and Advanced boards have a UEFI.
jsc.guide.firmware.fix1: No disk has a system yet, and no install medium is in a drive. Put one in, and start from it ([](jsc:installing)). The exact words depend on the era ([](jsc:no_bootable_device)).
jsc.guide.firmware.fix2: The disk is not connected to the computer, or the medium is in the wrong kind of drive. A floppy goes in a Floppy Drive and a CD in a CD Drive ([](jsc:drives)).
jsc.guide.firmware.fix3: Change the boot order on the Boot Order page of the Setup, or pick the disk in the Boot Menu ([](jsc:setup_utility)).
jsc.guide.firmware.problem1: The screen reports that nothing can start, in words that depend on the era.
jsc.guide.firmware.problem2: A disk is not in the list.
jsc.guide.firmware.problem3: The computer starts from the wrong disk.
jsc.guide.firmware.table1_1_2: Text BIOS, plain text on the screen.
jsc.guide.firmware.text1: The firmware lives on the motherboard, not on any disk, so it is there before any system. It is the first program that runs when the computer starts: it checks the hardware ([](jsc:turning_on)), finds the disks and drives, and hands the computer to a system. If no system is found, it waits on the screen for you.
jsc.guide.firmware.text2: Its kind depends on the era of the motherboard. Older boards have a BIOS, and newer boards have a UEFI. Both are firmware, and each era has its own look:
jsc.guide.firmware.text3: The boot order is the list of disks in the order the firmware tries them. You change the order on the Boot Order page of the Setup ([](jsc:setup_utility)).
jsc.guide.firmware.text4: The Boot Menu ([](jsc:boot_menu)) is the same choice for one start only. A disk you pick there is not saved, so the next start follows the boot order again.
jsc.guide.firmware.text5: A disk with two systems on it can show a menu before it starts. See [Two systems on one computer](jsc:two_systems).
jsc.guide.firmware.text6: The Setup also has a Hardware page, which lists what the firmware found in the machine. On a server with a storage controller, it has a Storage page for the array of its drives ([](jsc:raid_arrays)).
jsc.guide.firmware.title: Firmware: the BIOS and the UEFI
jsc.guide.firmware_for_install.definitio: The older kind of firmware, in text or with a blue panel. It starts a disk from the very first part of it.
A part of a disk that the system treats as a disk of its own. One disk can hold several of these parts.
The newer kind of firmware. It reads a small partition of the disk, formatted as FAT (File Allocation Table), to find the program that starts the system.
jsc.guide.firmware_for_install.fix1: The start program needs the FAT partition, mounted where that step says. Make the partition first, as the walkthrough's modern steps show ([](jsc:the_walkthrough)).
jsc.guide.firmware_for_install.problem1: The bootloader step refuses on a Standard or later computer.
jsc.guide.firmware_for_install.table1_1_: The whole disk: the start program goes on the disk itself.
jsc.guide.firmware_for_install.table1_2_: The whole disk: the start program goes on the disk itself.
jsc.guide.firmware_for_install.table1_3_: A small FAT partition for the start program, made in the disk steps.
jsc.guide.firmware_for_install.text1: The firmware comes in two kinds, and the era of your motherboard decides which one you have. The older kind is the basic input/output system (BIOS). The newer kind is the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI). The install needs the difference, because each kind starts a disk in its own way.
jsc.guide.firmware_for_install.text2: On a Vintage, Legacy or Transition computer the walkthrough is shorter. Its opening lines say so: "On older firmware the root is the whole disk, /dev/sda, and the steps that say so below are left out."
jsc.guide.firmware_for_install.text3: On a Standard or later computer, make the partition first. The walkthrough marks the steps for modern firmware, and you type them in order: a new table, a 512 MB partition, its type set to EFI System (type 1), and then the partition formatted as FAT. The chapter [The disks](jsc:preparing_disks) shows each step.
jsc.guide.firmware_for_install.text4: Both kinds take the same keys while the computer starts. [[DEL]] enters the Setup, the firmware's settings, and [[F12]] opens the Boot Menu ([](jsc:firmware)).
jsc.guide.firmware_for_install.title: BIOS or UEFI
jsc.guide.first_boot.definition1: The service manager of these systems. It starts the services at boot, in order.
jsc.guide.first_boot.definition2: The program that shows the graphical login and starts the desktop. Here it starts only when a desktop is installed.
jsc.guide.first_boot.definition3: The step where the system asks who is using the computer, before it starts a session for that user.
jsc.guide.first_boot.fix1: Install a desktop with apt install gnome on Ubuntu or Debian, or dnf install gnome on Fedora, then reboot. Cinnamon needs Standard hardware.
jsc.guide.first_boot.fix2: The computer is not on a network whose Mainframe runs the Mirror. Connect its data cable to that Mainframe ([](jsc:data_cables)).
jsc.guide.first_boot.problem1: The system starts at a shell, with no desktop.
jsc.guide.first_boot.problem2: The boot shows no "Found package mirror" line.
jsc.guide.first_boot.table1_10_2: Only when a desktop is installed, named in lower case: kde plasma, gnome or cinnamon.
jsc.guide.first_boot.table1_2_2: Always. On a 32-bit machine it reads i686.
jsc.guide.first_boot.table1_3_2: Always: the central processing unit (CPU) of the machine.
jsc.guide.first_boot.table1_4_2: Always: the memory of the machine.
jsc.guide.first_boot.table1_5_2: One line for each disk, with the letters sda, sdb and on.
jsc.guide.first_boot.table1_8_2: Only when a data cable joins the computer to a Mainframe.
jsc.guide.first_boot.table1_9_2: Only when that Mainframe runs the Mirror.
jsc.guide.first_boot.text1: When the installer has finished and the computer has rebooted, the installed system starts from its own disk. You see a list of lines as the kernel and the services start, then a login line on the text console, the first screen of the machine.
jsc.guide.first_boot.text2: The boot begins with "Loading Linux 6.8-jsc ..." and "Loading initial ramdisk ...". The lines that begin with "[  OK  ]" report that a service started. The system is run by systemd.
jsc.guide.first_boot.text3: Without a desktop there is no display manager line. The boot ends at the text console: a banner, a login and a shell, and nothing else.
jsc.guide.first_boot.text4: The text console prints a greeting, then waits at its login line. Here is the greeting on Ubuntu. Debian and Fedora print the same lines with their own name.
jsc.guide.first_boot.text5: The login is a line, and nothing checks the password you are asked for, because nothing in this world logs in with a password yet. You are always the user player.
jsc.guide.first_boot.title: The first boot
jsc.guide.first_computer.balloon2_detail: Press it to turn the computer on.
jsc.guide.first_computer.balloon4_detail: It joins the monitor to the computer when the monitor cannot stand against the case.
jsc.guide.first_computer.definition1: The floppy, CD, DVD or USB stick a system is installed from. The installer is the program on it.
jsc.guide.first_computer.figure1: A Personal Computer with its Monitor, joined by a Peripheral Cable. Drag it to see the back.
jsc.guide.first_computer.fix1: A build needs a motherboard, a processor, memory and a power supply. The tooltip also names a disk: put one in as well, so the computer has a system to start from.
jsc.guide.first_computer.fix2: The build is refused. Check the parts against each other: the socket, the era, the memory generation and the power ([](jsc:build_refusals)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.fix3: Put the monitor right against the case, or lay a Peripheral Cable between them ([](jsc:peripheral_cables)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.fix4: Put a graphics card in the case, or use a processor with graphics built in ([](jsc:graphics_cards)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.fix5: Press the power button on the front of the case ([](jsc:case_front)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.fix6: A part is missing or does not fit. Open the computer: its CHECKS list names what to fix ([](jsc:build_refusals)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.fix7: Check the board: the socket, the era and the memory generation must match ([](jsc:motherboards)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.fix8: No system is on a disk yet. Install one ([](jsc:installing)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.problem1: The window's tooltip says "Not a computer yet".
jsc.guide.first_computer.problem2: The switch goes on, but the computer does not run.
jsc.guide.first_computer.problem3: The monitor says "No computer found in range over a Peripheral Cable".
jsc.guide.first_computer.problem4: The monitor says "The computer has no video output: install a graphics card".
jsc.guide.first_computer.problem5: The monitor says "No signal - the computer is powered off".
jsc.guide.first_computer.problem6: The computer beeps, and the monitor says that its parts do not make a computer.
jsc.guide.first_computer.problem7: A processor or a memory module does not go into its slot.
jsc.guide.first_computer.problem8: The firmware reports that no system can start.
jsc.guide.first_computer.step1: Put a motherboard in. It is the board the other parts sit on, and the case takes only a board of its own era ([](jsc:motherboards)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.step2: Put a processor in. Its socket must match the board's socket ([](jsc:processors)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.step3: Put memory in. The board takes some kinds of memory and not others ([](jsc:memory)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.step4: Put a graphics card in. Without one the monitor has no picture, unless the processor has graphics built in ([](jsc:graphics_cards)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.step5: Put a disk in. The system is installed on it, and your files are kept on it ([](jsc:disks)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.step6: Put a power supply in. It gives the parts their power, rated in watts (W) ([](jsc:power_supplies)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.step7: Put the install medium of Frames 10 in the Dock Station.
jsc.guide.first_computer.step8: Turn the computer on, and watch the monitor ([](jsc:turning_on)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.step9: Start the installer from the medium, and follow it ([](jsc:installing)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.text1: Building a computer is easier than it sounds. You place a case, put the parts in it one by one, and then you add a monitor.
jsc.guide.first_computer.text10: Press the power button on the front of the case ([](jsc:case_front)). The monitor shows the start-up, and if no system is on any disk, the firmware waits for you ([](jsc:no_bootable_device)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.text11: Once the computer runs, the monitor's power strip offers the buttons Shut down the PC and Restart the PC.
jsc.guide.first_computer.text2: Take a Personal Computer from the creative tab J's Computers - Standard and place it. Using the computer opens its window, which is the inside of the case, with one place for each part. A case on its own does nothing yet.
jsc.guide.first_computer.text3: A computer with no disk still switches on, and then it reports that no system can start ([](jsc:no_bootable_device)). A computer with no motherboard or no power supply has no build at all, so it stays off.
jsc.guide.first_computer.text4: A part that does not fit does not go into its slot. A processor or a memory module must match the board's socket, era and memory generation. A graphics card must fit the board's bus.
jsc.guide.first_computer.text5: A power supply with a fixed wattage refuses the build when the parts draw more watts than it gives. The switch goes on, but the computer does not run.
jsc.guide.first_computer.text6: On a Personal Computer, the window only says that it is not a computer yet, and what it still needs. The assembly screen of a server lists each problem in its tooltip.
jsc.guide.first_computer.text7: A computer with no screen is not much use. Place a Monitor ([](jsc:monitors)) right against the case, and it is joined to the computer. Lay a [Peripheral Cable](jsc:peripheral_cables) when the monitor has to stand further away.
jsc.guide.first_computer.text8: The Dock Station ([](jsc:dock_station)) reads USB sticks, and that is where a USB install medium goes. Join it to the computer like any other drive.
jsc.guide.first_computer.text9: The system and its programs show on the monitor, not in the window. The front of the case has the power button ([](jsc:case_front)).
jsc.guide.first_computer.title: Building your first computer
jsc.guide.first_network.balloon1_detail: It runs the network. Join the backbone cable to any side of it.
jsc.guide.first_network.balloon2_detail: Run it from the router to the Mainframe.
jsc.guide.first_network.balloon3_detail: Join the access cable and the backbone cable to it.
jsc.guide.first_network.balloon4_detail: Run it from the computer to the router.
jsc.guide.first_network.balloon5_detail: Plug the access cable into its back.
jsc.guide.first_network.figure1: A Mainframe, a router, data cables and a Personal Computer: the smallest network. Drag it to see the back.
jsc.guide.first_network.fix1: Its cable is longer than its range, or of another era than the router. Add a repeater, or a router of the newer era.
jsc.guide.first_network.fix2: No Mainframe is on the computer's network. Follow the cables from the computer to the Mainframe ([](jsc:data_cables)).
jsc.guide.first_network.fix3: The Mainframe has no system, so it holds every Operation until one is installed ([](jsc:installing)).
jsc.guide.first_network.fix4: Put an Optical Network Card in the Mainframe's card slots ([](jsc:expansion_cards)), and mount a Fibre Optic Interface in the rack ([](jsc:rack_equipment)).
jsc.guide.first_network.problem1: A computer is not on the network.
jsc.guide.first_network.problem2: The Network program says "○ Mainframe offline".
jsc.guide.first_network.problem3: Nothing goes into storage, and every Operation stays queued.
jsc.guide.first_network.problem4: The fibre does not join the Mainframe or the rack.
jsc.guide.first_network.step1: Build a Mainframe and give it its parts: an MTX motherboard, a power supply, processors, memory, a disk and a graphics card ([](jsc:mainframes)).
jsc.guide.first_network.step2: Install a system on the Mainframe, such as MC-NET, as on any computer: a monitor on its graphics card, and the install medium in a drive joined to it ([](jsc:installing)). A Mainframe without a system runs nothing.
jsc.guide.first_network.step3: Build a Server Rack and put servers with disks in its bays ([](jsc:server_racks)).
jsc.guide.first_network.step4: Join the Mainframe and the rack with the backbone cable of their era: HBW in the Legacy, Fibre Optic in the Standard. Fibre goes into the Mainframe only while it holds an Optical Network Card ([](jsc:expansion_cards)), and into the rack only through a Fibre Optic Interface mounted in it ([](jsc:rack_equipment)).
jsc.guide.first_network.step5: Place a router, and join your Personal Computer to it with the access cable, Ethernet or Gigabit ([](jsc:routers)). Run the backbone from the router to the Mainframe.
jsc.guide.first_network.step6: At the computer, open the Network program ([](jsc:network_interactor)). Put items in, and they are stored on the servers' disks; ask for them back, and they come out.
jsc.guide.first_network.text1: Here is the smallest network that does something useful.
jsc.guide.first_network.text2: The Mainframe joins every data cable that touches any side of its footprint, so a backbone can meet it on whichever side is nearest. Fibre is the one cable it takes only with the card.
jsc.guide.first_network.text3: That is it. From here everything else is more of the same: more racks for more storage, more computers on the access line, a Crafting Computer for autocrafting.
jsc.guide.first_network.title: Your first network
jsc.guide.first_queries.definition1: A computer on the network that holds items on its disks.
jsc.guide.first_queries.definition2: A list that a QUERY reads, such as disks, servers or items.
jsc.guide.first_queries.fix1: Write the item's name after the action, such as iron_ingot.
jsc.guide.first_queries.fix10: No server has that name. Use QUERY servers to see the names.
jsc.guide.first_queries.fix11: Name what to query after QUERY, such as disks or items.
jsc.guide.first_queries.fix12: The network has no pattern for that item ([](jsc:how_autocrafting_works)).
jsc.guide.first_queries.fix13: The Midsoft IQL Server is stopped. Start it with iqlengine start.
jsc.guide.first_queries.fix2: Write a number of items instead, such as 50 items.
jsc.guide.first_queries.fix3: SELECT brings items to you. Leave out TO. To send items between two places, use MOVE.
jsc.guide.first_queries.fix4: Add TO, followed by the place where the items go.
jsc.guide.first_queries.fix5: Give both places, FROM where the items come from and TO where they go.
jsc.guide.first_queries.fix6: A query only reads. Leave out FROM, or use an action that moves items.
jsc.guide.first_queries.fix7: Use one of the levels the reply lists: LOW, MEDIUM_LOW, MEDIUM, MEDIUM_HIGH or HIGH.
jsc.guide.first_queries.fix8: Check the spelling of the action word. The words that exist are in [the catalogue](jsc:operations_catalogue).
jsc.guide.first_queries.fix9: The network does not know that name. Check the spelling, or write the full name, such as minecraft:iron_ingot.
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem1: The reply says "syntax: expected an item".
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem10: The reply says "no server named", followed by the name.
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem11: The reply says "syntax: expected an object to query".
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem12: The reply says "no pattern crafts", followed by the item's name.
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem13: The reply says "Network Operations Service unavailable".
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem14: The reply says "the network has no running Mainframe".
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem2: The reply says "syntax: percentage quantities are not supported yet".
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem3: The reply says "syntax: SELECT has no TO destination".
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem4: The reply says "syntax: DELETE exports out of the network and needs a TO destination".
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem5: The reply says "syntax: MOVE is internal and needs both FROM and TO".
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem6: The reply says "syntax: FROM is not valid on a read".
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem7: The reply says "syntax: unknown priority level".
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem8: The reply says "syntax: unknown verb", followed by a word.
jsc.guide.first_queries.problem9: The reply says "unknown item", followed by the name.
jsc.guide.first_queries.step1: Join the computer to the network with a data cable ([](jsc:first_network)).
jsc.guide.first_queries.step4: Type iql SELECT 64 iron_ingot and press [[Enter]].
jsc.guide.first_queries.step5: Read the reply: it says the SELECT is queued, and where the items go.
jsc.guide.first_queries.step6: Type iql CRAFT 64 torch and press [[Enter]].
jsc.guide.first_queries.step7: Read the reply: it says the CRAFT is queued.
jsc.guide.first_queries.table1_1_2: A row for each disk, or "no rows"
jsc.guide.first_queries.table1_3_2: The items held in amounts over 100
jsc.guide.first_queries.table1_4_2: The 2 rows with the largest quantity
jsc.guide.first_queries.text1: This entry takes you from a network with nothing typed yet to your first answers and your first work. Each step shows what you type and what the network says back. If your reply differs, read the problems at the end.
jsc.guide.first_queries.text2: The reply says "Midsoft IQL Server: running" when the server is ready to answer. If it says stopped, start it with iqlengine start ([](jsc:engine_services)).
jsc.guide.first_queries.text3: Type net to see a summary of the whole network. It has headings for the network, the Mainframe, the servers, the computers, the subframes and the types it indexes.
jsc.guide.first_queries.text4: Each row is one line. Its name and details are on the left, and its quantity is on the right. The command line shows at most 64 rows, so a longer answer is cut short.
jsc.guide.first_queries.text5: The three tables of these first reads have these fields. Each field is one piece of information about a row.
jsc.guide.first_queries.text6: ORDER BY sorts the rows by one field before they are shown. DESC reverses the order. LIMIT 2 stops the answer after 2 rows. The other tables are listed in [QUERY and SELECT](jsc:query_and_select).
jsc.guide.first_queries.text7: SELECT with no FROM takes the items from anywhere on the network. To take them from one server, write FROM and the server's name, as QUERY servers lists it. The reply names the item by its display name, and the items reach local storage: this computer's own storage.
jsc.guide.first_queries.text8: CRAFT makes items, and it works only for items the network has a pattern for ([](jsc:how_autocrafting_works)).
jsc.guide.first_queries.text9: Type interac ops at the prompt to list the work that is still running. The Network Manager program also lists the Operations in flight ([](jsc:network_manager)).
jsc.guide.first_queries.title: Your first queries, step by step
jsc.guide.fluids.definition1: One thousandth of a bucket. Fluids and chemicals are counted in these, and each one takes one thousandth of an item's room.
jsc.guide.fluids.definition2: A substance that a mod such as Mekanism keeps in its own tanks.
jsc.guide.fluids.definition3: The piece of this mod that teaches the network how to read a chemical mod's tanks.
jsc.guide.fluids.fix1: The network's storage has no room left. Add disks or servers ([](jsc:storage_trouble)).
jsc.guide.fluids.fix2: Install Mekanism. The network reads chemicals only through it.
jsc.guide.fluids.problem1: The fluid does not go in.
jsc.guide.fluids.problem2: No chemical shows in the network's storage.
jsc.guide.fluids.table1_1_2: Gives up its whole 1,000 mB, or nothing. The empty bucket comes back.
jsc.guide.fluids.table1_2_2: Gives up as much as fits, up to what the item allows at once. The emptied tank comes back.
jsc.guide.fluids.text1: The network keeps fluids the way it keeps items: as data, counted in millibuckets (mB). A bucket holds 1,000 millibuckets, so a full bucket takes exactly as much room as one item ([](jsc:items_as_data)).
jsc.guide.fluids.text2: An External Storage Bus can face a tank of any mod. The network then uses the tank's fluid as storage, as it does with items.
jsc.guide.fluids.text3: Fluid also comes in and goes out in containers. You can use a bucket or a tank for it, and each behaves its own way.
jsc.guide.fluids.text4: Taking fluid out works the other way. A bucket is filled only with a full bucket's worth. Any fluid the network could not take goes back into the container.
jsc.guide.fluids.text5: Chemicals take room in millibuckets, like a fluid. They need Mekanism: install it, and a chemical bridge lets the network read its chemical tanks ([](jsc:mekanism)).
jsc.guide.fluids.title: Fluids and chemicals
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.definition1: To erase every file on a drive and prepare the drive again.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.definition2: The disk as the machine sees it, with the files on it.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.fix1: C: holds the running system. Format a second drive instead ([](jsc:drives)).
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.fix2: Link a disk to that drive ([](jsc:drives)), then try again.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.fix3: Check the drive letter and the warning before you add /y.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.problem1: format says it cannot format drive C:.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.problem2: format says the drive is not ready.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.step1: Type format, a space, the drive letter and a colon, such as D:.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.step2: Read the warning. It names the drive that will be erased.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.step3: Type the same line with /y at the end, such as format D: /y, to start the format.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.table1_1_2: You typed format with no drive.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.table1_2_2: The first word is not a drive letter.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.table1_3_1: format: drive D: drive not ready
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.table1_3_2: No disk is in that drive.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.table1_4_2: No drive of that letter is linked to the computer.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.table1_5_1: format: cannot format drive C: - the running system lives on it
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.table1_5_2: The system disk cannot be formatted from its own prompt.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.table1_6_2: The drive is formatted. The next line says: All data on the volume was erased.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.text1: Formatting erases everything on a drive and prepares the drive again to hold files. Use it on a new disk, or on a disk whose files you no longer need.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.text2: format asks for /y before it does anything. Without it, format prints the warning in red, then the dim line that shows the line to type. The erasing itself needs the /y.
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.title: Formatting a drive
jsc.guide.format_a_drive.warning1: Formatting erases every file on the drive, and there is no undo. Check the drive letter before you run the line.
jsc.guide.frames_10.definition1: A square in the Start list that can show a changing value.
jsc.guide.frames_10.definition2: The button that shows every open window.
jsc.guide.frames_10.definition3: The panel at the right edge of the screen that gathers the notices.
jsc.guide.frames_10.fix1: A Legacy computer cannot run Frames 10. Frames XP runs on it ([](jsc:frames_xp)).
jsc.guide.frames_10.fix2: A Transition computer cannot run Frames 10. Frames 7 runs on it ([](jsc:frames_7)).
jsc.guide.frames_10.problem1: The installer says "Frames 10 needs Standard era hardware or newer; this machine is Legacy era."
jsc.guide.frames_10.problem2: The installer says "Frames 10 needs Standard era hardware or newer; this machine is Transition era."
jsc.guide.frames_10.step1: Put the Frames 10 install stick in the Dock Station ([](jsc:dock_station)).
jsc.guide.frames_10.step2: Start the computer from the stick. If the computer does not start from it, open the Boot Menu ([](jsc:boot_menu)).
jsc.guide.frames_10.step3: Choose a disk on the disk page.
jsc.guide.frames_10.step4: Wait while the installer goes through "Copying Frames files", "Getting files ready for installation", "Installing features", "Installing updates" and "Finishing up".
jsc.guide.frames_10.step5: Answer the question "Who's going to use this PC?".
jsc.guide.frames_10.text1: Frames 10 is the fourth edition. You need a Standard computer or newer, and it installs from a USB stick that goes in the [Dock Station](jsc:dock_station). Its footprint is 16,384 MB, which is 64 items on a Standard disk.
jsc.guide.frames_10.text2: Its look is Metro: a dark taskbar with a search box and a task view beside the Start button. Start is a list with live tiles, and the Action Center sits at the right edge of the screen.
jsc.guide.frames_10.text3: The file program is called File Explorer. Help is called Get Help, and its window is called Get Help too.
jsc.guide.frames_10.text4: The installer is a white window with a thin blue border over a dark ground. When you reach the set-up that follows, it fills the screen in blue.
jsc.guide.frames_10.text5: Its Task Manager is the modern form, with the pages Processes, Performance, Services, Storage, Network and GPU. The GPU page is described in [Frames 11](jsc:frames_11).
jsc.guide.frames_10.text6: Its Device Manager is flat: the modern form that Frames 11 kept.
jsc.guide.frames_10.text7: Personalize > Effects holds the visual effects. Its note reads "How Frames looks and moves. A weak graphics card turns both off by itself." The page has two switches: "Transparency effects" and "Play animations in Frames".
jsc.guide.frames_10.text8: On a new computer, Frames 10 says "Hi.", the first edition of the family to do so. It plays "Frames 10 chimes" when it starts.
jsc.guide.frames_10.text9: Its splash screen is black, with a window of four panes in blue, and a ring of dots chases round below it. It has no error sound of its own: when something goes wrong it plays the Frames 11 error sound, "Frames 11 error".
jsc.guide.frames_10.title: Frames 10
jsc.guide.frames_10.value1_2: USB stick, in the Dock Station
jsc.guide.frames_11.definition1: The shell of Frames 11: the program that takes your commands, under its own name on that edition.
jsc.guide.frames_11.definition2: Tiling a window against an edge of the screen when you let go of it there.
jsc.guide.frames_11.definition3: The part of the screen that the taskbar does not cover.
jsc.guide.frames_11.definition4: The memory on a graphics card, which the monitors and the graphics windows use.
jsc.guide.frames_11.fix1: Only the edges in the table snap a window. Drag the window to one of them, and let go.
jsc.guide.frames_11.fix2: Frames 10 has no edge snapping. Move and resize the window by hand.
jsc.guide.frames_11.fix3: Install a graphics card in the computer ([](jsc:graphics_cards)).
jsc.guide.frames_11.fix4: Turn off a monitor, or use a card with more memory ([](jsc:graphics_cards)).
jsc.guide.frames_11.fix5: Turn off a monitor or close a graphics program.
jsc.guide.frames_11.fix6: The computer has no graphics card and no graphics on its processor. Install a graphics card ([](jsc:graphics_cards)).
jsc.guide.frames_11.problem1: A window let go in the middle of the screen does not tile.
jsc.guide.frames_11.problem2: A window does not tile on Frames 10.
jsc.guide.frames_11.problem3: The monitor says "The computer has no video output: install a graphics card".
jsc.guide.frames_11.problem4: The monitor stays dark and says "Not enough video memory". It lights when the card has room.
jsc.guide.frames_11.problem5: A graphics window does not open, and the desktop says "Not enough video memory".
jsc.guide.frames_11.problem6: The GPU page says "This computer has no graphics."
jsc.guide.frames_11.step1: Put the Frames 11 USB stick in the Dock Station, and start the computer from it. If the computer does not start from it, open the Boot Menu ([](jsc:boot_menu)).
jsc.guide.frames_11.step2: On the page "Where do you want to install Frames 11?", choose a disk.
jsc.guide.frames_11.step3: On the page "Name this PC", give the computer a name.
jsc.guide.frames_11.step4: Wait while the copy shows "Copying files", "Creating the system folders", "Adding the built-in programs" and "Setting up the boot entry" in turn, under the caption "Installing Frames 11".
jsc.guide.frames_11.table2_1_1: Within 4 pixels of the top of the work area
jsc.guide.frames_11.table2_1_2: The window maximises, and fills the work area.
jsc.guide.frames_11.table2_2_1: Within 4 pixels of the left edge of the screen
jsc.guide.frames_11.table2_2_2: The window fills the left half of the work area.
jsc.guide.frames_11.table2_3_1: Within 4 pixels of the right edge of the screen
jsc.guide.frames_11.table2_3_2: The window fills the right half of the work area.
jsc.guide.frames_11.table2_4_2: The window stays where you let it go.
jsc.guide.frames_11.table3_1_2: GPU, and the card's name on the right in small text.
jsc.guide.frames_11.table3_2_2: How busy the card is, from 0 to 100.
jsc.guide.frames_11.table3_3_2: How full the memory is: "Dedicated GPU memory usage" for a card, or "Shared GPU memory usage" for integrated graphics.
jsc.guide.frames_11.table3_4_2: How busy the card is, as a percent.
jsc.guide.frames_11.table3_5_2: The memory in use, out of the total.
jsc.guide.frames_11.table3_6_2: The number of cores, and the clock speed in MHz or GHz.
jsc.guide.frames_11.table3_7_2: The PCI Express (PCIe) slot the card sits in, or "On the processor" for integrated graphics.
jsc.guide.frames_11.table3_8_2: One row for each monitor or graphics window that holds video memory, with its size.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text1: Frames 11 is the newest edition, the fifth. It needs an Advanced computer, the newest era with parts, and it needs the most room of the family: 20,480 MB, which is 80 items on an Advanced disk.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text10: Edge snapping tiles a window against an edge of the screen. It works on Frames 11 and on the KDE, GNOME and Cinnamon desktops of the Linux systems ([](jsc:unix_desktops)). Frames 95, XP, 7 and 10 do not snap.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text11: Where you let go decides what the window does. A window within 4 pixels of an edge changes its size and place:
jsc.guide.frames_11.text12: Snapping happens when you let go, not while you drag. Keep the window at the edge, and then release the mouse button.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text13: A window that you snap keeps its old place. When you restore it from maximised, it returns to where it was before the snap.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text14: The GPU page is in Task Manager, and it shows the graphics processing unit (GPU) of the computer: the card that draws the picture for the monitors. Frames 10 has the same page. It shows how busy the card is, and which monitors and windows use its video memory.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text15: The page shows the first graphics card in the computer's build. With no card, it shows the graphics of the processor, if the processor has any, and the memory is then shared with the computer.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text16: The utilisation percentage grows with two things. The memory fill adds up to 50 percent, and each open graphics window adds 20 percent. It is 0 when no video memory is in use, and it never goes above 100 percent.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text17: A lit monitor holds video memory in blocks, and a graphics window takes a quarter of a monitor block, or a whole block while it fills the screen. A block's size depends on the era of the computer.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text18: These sizes are estimates. The table gives the 16-colour block; a Vintage monitor that shows only black and white uses 64 KB per block. The page writes an amount in KB below 1 MB, in MB below 1 GB, and in GB above that, with one decimal place.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text2: It installs from a USB stick in the [Dock Station](jsc:dock_station), and it keeps 8,192 MB of RAM for itself.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text3: The installer's pages are pale cards, with one question to a page.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text4: Its look is Modern: a dark taskbar, centred along the bottom of the screen, and a Start menu that floats above it, with a search box and a pinned grid of programs.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text5: The file program is called File Explorer, as on Frames 10.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text6: Its Device Manager has the flat modern form. The visual effects are under Personalize > Visual effects, with one switch, "Animation effects". Its note reads "Windows open, close and minimize with motion, flyouts slide".
jsc.guide.frames_11.text7: On a new computer, Frames 11 says "Hi.", as Frames 10 does. It plays "Frames 11 chimes" when it starts and "Frames 11 error" when something goes wrong. Its splash screen is near black, with the maker's mark in the middle and a ring of dots turning below.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text8: Frames 11 has its own shell, under the name Megashell. Frames 95, XP, 7 and 10 call it Command Prompt, and on Frames 11 its window and its name on the desktop are Megashell.
jsc.guide.frames_11.text9: For the commands you type, see [The Command Prompt](jsc:command_prompt). Help on this edition opens the Get Help window ([](jsc:help_on_a_computer)).
jsc.guide.frames_11.title: Frames 11
jsc.guide.frames_11.value1_2: USB stick, in the Dock Station
jsc.guide.frames_7.definition1: A taskbar made of icons with no titles, as on Frames 7.
jsc.guide.frames_7.fix1: A Legacy computer cannot run Frames 7. Frames XP runs on it ([](jsc:frames_xp)).
jsc.guide.frames_7.problem1: The installer says "Frames 7 needs Transition era hardware or newer; this machine is Legacy era."
jsc.guide.frames_7.step1: Put the Frames 7 DVD in the DVD Drive, and start the computer from it. If the computer does not start from it, open the Boot Menu ([](jsc:boot_menu)).
jsc.guide.frames_7.step2: Choose a disk on the disk page.
jsc.guide.frames_7.step3: Wait while the installer goes through "Copying Frames files", "Expanding Frames files", "Installing features", "Installing updates" and "Completing installation".
jsc.guide.frames_7.step4: Type a name for the computer on the page that says "Choose a name for your computer to distinguish it on the network."
jsc.guide.frames_7.text1: Frames 7 is the third edition. You need a Transition computer or newer, and it installs from a digital versatile disc (DVD) in the DVD Drive. Its footprint is 16,384 MB, which is 64 items on a Transition disk.
jsc.guide.frames_7.text2: Its look is the glass look. The taskbar is a superbar, and its icons have no titles. Start is a round orb, and a show-desktop button sits at the right edge of the taskbar.
jsc.guide.frames_7.text3: The Start menu has two columns, and one of them is a glass panel of places. On Frames 7 the program This PC is called Computer, and the Settings program is called Control Panel.
jsc.guide.frames_7.text4: Frames 7 calls its help program Help and Support. Its window is called "Frames Help and Support" and has a "Search Help" box.
jsc.guide.frames_7.text5: Its Task Manager has the four tabs of Frames XP, and its Device Manager is the console of Frames XP, in glass.
jsc.guide.frames_7.text6: Its Performance Options page is reached from System, as on Frames XP, with the same visual effects and one more check: "Enable transparent glass". Under the heading "Ease of Access: make the computer easier to see" is a switch, "Turn off all unnecessary animations (when possible)".
jsc.guide.frames_7.text7: On a new computer, Frames 7 shows its own Welcome, not "Hi.". It plays "Frames 7 chimes" when it starts. Its error sound is Frames XP's, "Frames XP error".
jsc.guide.frames_7.text8: Its splash screen is black: four coloured lights sweep in and close into a waving flag, with the name of the system under it.
jsc.guide.frames_7.title: Frames 7
jsc.guide.frames_95.definition1: A way of running programs in which each program keeps the processor until it gives it up.
jsc.guide.frames_95.fix1: A Vintage computer cannot run Frames 95, so if you have one, use a Legacy computer or newer ([](jsc:eras)).
jsc.guide.frames_95.fix2: Run that program on a computer with Frames XP or newer ([](jsc:frames_xp)).
jsc.guide.frames_95.problem1: The installer says "Frames 95 needs Legacy era hardware or newer; this machine is Vintage era."
jsc.guide.frames_95.problem2: A program says "Automation Manager needs Frames XP or newer. This computer runs Frames 95."
jsc.guide.frames_95.step1: Put the Frames 95 CD in the CD Drive, and start the computer from it. If the computer does not start from it, open the Boot Menu ([](jsc:boot_menu)).
jsc.guide.frames_95.step2: Wait while the installer checks the computer: "Setup is checking this computer before it starts."
jsc.guide.frames_95.step3: Choose a disk on the page "Choose a Disk".
jsc.guide.frames_95.step4: Give the computer a name on the page "Computer Name".
jsc.guide.frames_95.step5: Wait on the page "Copying Files" until the copy is done.
jsc.guide.frames_95.text1: Frames 95 is the oldest edition and the first of the family. It needs a Legacy computer or newer, and it installs from a compact disc (CD) in the CD Drive.
jsc.guide.frames_95.text2: Its look is the classic one: a grey taskbar with bevelled edges, and a Start list in a band down one side of the screen.
jsc.guide.frames_95.text3: Frames 95 is cooperative. Each program keeps the processor until it gives it up, and the system does not take it back. Frames XP and the later editions are preemptive instead: the system takes the processor back when a program's turn is over.
jsc.guide.frames_95.text4: The installer is a grey wizard, with a picture down one side, that moves through those pages in order.
jsc.guide.frames_95.text5: Frames 95 names its help program Help. Its window is called "Help Topics: Frames Help" and has three tabs: Contents, Index and Find. A topic opens in a window called "Frames Help".
jsc.guide.frames_95.text6: On this edition the Device Manager is called System, and it sits inside the System dialog. Its Task Manager is a Close Program box.
jsc.guide.frames_95.text7: The visual effects page has the heading "Visual effects" and one check box: "Animate windows when minimizing and restoring".
jsc.guide.frames_95.text8: When Frames 95 starts it plays "Frames 95 chimes", and when something goes wrong it plays "Frames 95 error". It plays no sound when a device connects or disconnects.
jsc.guide.frames_95.text9: On a new computer, Frames 95 does not say "Hi.": it shows its own Welcome. When it starts, the screen shows a sky with the logo over the horizon, and a bar runs along the foot.
jsc.guide.frames_95.title: Frames 95
jsc.guide.frames_help.definition1: One page of help. On Frames 95 each topic opens in its own window.
jsc.guide.frames_help.fix1: Try a shorter word, or the name of the command.
jsc.guide.frames_help.fix2: Look for the command on a machine that has it.
jsc.guide.frames_help.problem1: The result line reads "Nothing in the manuals or the commands answers to", followed by your word.
jsc.guide.frames_help.problem2: A command you expected is missing from the results.
jsc.guide.frames_help.step1: Type the word you want. The search field opens as you type.
jsc.guide.frames_help.step3: Read the result line: it gives the number of results and the word you searched for.
jsc.guide.frames_help.table1_1_3: Tabs for Contents, Index and Find
jsc.guide.frames_help.table1_2_3: A Technical Reference pane, with Search, Home, Index, Favorites and History
jsc.guide.frames_help.table1_4_3: A search box that says "Search the manuals and commands"
jsc.guide.frames_help.table2_1_2: Goes back to the page before.
jsc.guide.frames_help.table2_3_2: Goes back, or deletes a letter while you type a search.
jsc.guide.frames_help.table2_5_2: Runs the search. On Frames 95 it displays the selected topic.
jsc.guide.frames_help.text1: Help is the window that reads the manuals of the series and the machine's own manual pages. Open it when you want to know what a command does or how a part works. Every desktop ships it, under a name that depends on the edition.
jsc.guide.frames_help.text2: The contents hold the manuals of the series, with the Technical Reference first, as books of chapters, sections and entries. The commands of the machine are there too: each command's page is the one the machine prints for it at a terminal.
jsc.guide.frames_help.text3: Links on a page lead to another page, and Back returns you to the page before.
jsc.guide.frames_help.text4: The help is read at this machine, so the page for a command shows only the commands the machine has.
jsc.guide.frames_help.title: Help and Support, and Get Help
jsc.guide.frames_memory.definition1: The part of the system that runs the programs and switches between them.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.definition2: A kernel in which each program must give the processor back by itself, because nothing forces it to.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.definition3: A kernel that switches programs by force, so that one program cannot hold the processor.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.definition4: The small notice that appears in the notification area of the desktop.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.definition5: The state of a machine that holds less than twice its system's own RAM.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.fix1: A program needed more memory than was free. Close a program before you open another one, or add RAM ([](jsc:memory)).
jsc.guide.frames_memory.fix2: The memory is past nine tenths. Close a program, or add RAM to the computer ([](jsc:memory)).
jsc.guide.frames_memory.fix3: A part was taken out while the computer ran. Put it back, and switch the computer on again if its monitor went dark.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.fix4: Turn off a monitor, or close a graphics program.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.fix5: The machine is tight on RAM. Add RAM until it holds at least twice the system's own RAM, using the table above.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.heading4: Tight RAM and the boot time
jsc.guide.frames_memory.problem1: The computer reboots after a blue crash page.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.problem4: A balloon says "Not enough video memory".
jsc.guide.frames_memory.problem5: The computer takes a long time to start.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.table1: What happens as the memory fills
jsc.guide.frames_memory.table1_1_3: The system crashes, with no warning.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.table1_2_3: A balloon warns once the memory passes nine tenths. Then the system crashes on the program that does not fit.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.table2: Memory below which each edition is tight
jsc.guide.frames_memory.text1: Setup does not refuse a machine for having little memory. Its check page shows your Memory line, and a machine with little memory can still take a Frames install. It then runs tight and boots slowly, as the section on tight RAM explains below.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.text10: A machine is tight for a system when it holds less than twice the system's own RAM. A tight boot takes one and a half times as long. You can see the limit for each edition in the table.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.text11: A boot takes about one second, plus the system's footprint in megabytes divided by (160 times the disk's speed times the machine's era factor). The disk's speed is 1 for a hard disk, 4 for a solid-state drive (SSD) and 16 for an NVMe drive. The era factor is 2 for Legacy, 3 for Transition, 4 for Standard and 8 for Advanced. The result is at least 2 seconds and at most 20 seconds.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.text12: With enough RAM, on a hard disk, Frames XP on a Legacy machine boots in about 6 seconds, and Frames 11 on an Advanced machine in about 17 seconds. Frames 7 on a Transition machine and Frames 10 on a Standard machine reach the 20-second limit.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.text2: The system keeps its own RAM first, before anything else: 32 MB for Frames 95, 128 MB for XP, 1 GB for 7, 3 GB for 10 and 8 GB for Frames 11 ([](jsc:frames_which_machine)). Every window you open takes memory too: its program's own RAM.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.text3: What a program holds grows with the era of the machine it runs on, because software grew with the machines it was written for. The figure a program gives is what it holds on a Legacy machine. It holds a sixteenth of that on a Vintage machine, 8 times as much on a Transition machine, 32 times on a Standard machine and 128 times on an Advanced machine. A program that comes with the system holds 16 MB on a Legacy machine. A typical machine of each era, with two memory sticks of the middle size, holds its system and about eight programs.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.text4: Free memory is the machine's total minus everything held. When a program needs more than is free, every Frames edition crashes: it does not refuse the program. This is true for a window, for a program started at the prompt and for a service. The newer editions warn first, as the table shows.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.text5: On Frames XP, 7, 10 and 11, the window that takes the memory past nine tenths opens with a balloon that says "Low on memory". Its text asks you to close some programs, and names the three that hold the most, with what each holds.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.text6: Each edition goes down on its own page. Frames 95 shows "A fatal exception has occurred.". XP and 7 show a stop error named MEMORY_MANAGEMENT. Frames 10 and 11 show a sad face, a code you can scan, and the stop code MEMORY_MANAGEMENT.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.text7: The page is on every monitor that shows the computer, and keys and clicks do nothing while it stands. The programs the computer ran stop. The page stays for 4.2 seconds on Frames 95, 6 seconds on XP, 8 seconds on 7 and 10 seconds on 10 and 11. Then the computer starts over from its self-test, into an empty session.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.text8: A part taken out of a running computer brings the system down too: a stick of memory, an expansion card, or the disk the system runs from. Frames shows the same page in red, and Frames 10 and 11 name the part. If the computer still has what it needs to run, it starts over after the page. If it does not, the monitor goes dark. Taking out the processor, the board or the power supply switches the computer off at once, with no page.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.text9: Graphics programs also need video memory. When a window needs more than is free, the balloon says "Not enough video memory" and asks you to turn off a monitor or close a graphics program.
jsc.guide.frames_memory.title: Memory and the Frames editions
jsc.guide.frames_program_list.definition: A set of instructions the machine runs for you.
A program that comes with the edition, with no install step.
A program that is not on the machine at first: you install it from a medium or from the Mirror.
jsc.guide.frames_program_list.fix1: It is not a bundled desktop program. Right-click the taskbar and choose Task Manager ([](jsc:task_manager)).
jsc.guide.frames_program_list.fix2: It is an installable program: install it first ([](jsc:programs)).
jsc.guide.frames_program_list.problem1: The Task Manager is not on the desktop.
jsc.guide.frames_program_list.problem2: Virtual Studio is not in the list.
jsc.guide.frames_program_list.text1: Every Frames edition comes with the same core set of programs, so the tools you need are on each one. They are This PC, Settings, Files, the Editor, the Command Prompt, System Monitor, Calculator, the Device Manager, Help, and the Network and the Network Manager.
jsc.guide.frames_program_list.text2: Most of what you need is built in, but not all of it: Virtual Studio is installable.
jsc.guide.frames_program_list.text3: Some editions give the same program a name of their own. The Files window is called File Explorer on Frames 10 and 11, and the This PC window is called Computer on Frames 7. The table shows how the names of Files, This PC and Help change from edition to edition.
jsc.guide.frames_program_list.text4: On Frames 7 the Control Panel is the name of Settings. On Frames 11 the launcher calls the prompt Megashell, which is the Command Prompt ([](jsc:command_prompt)) under another name.
jsc.guide.frames_program_list.title: The programs of Frames
jsc.guide.frames_settings.definition1: The first page of Settings on Frames 7 and Frames 10, which lists the categories or the tiles.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.definition2: Five scores that rate the processor, the memory, the graphics, the gaming and the disk of a computer.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.definition3: The highlight colour of the desktop, used for selections and buttons.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.definition4: A named preset that sets the accent and the wallpaper together.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.fix1: The Users page is not built yet, so the game shows that note.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.fix2: The button shows only when a monitor is linked to the computer. Link a monitor, then open the System page again.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.fix3: Link speakers to the computer's sound output, then look at the page again.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.fix4: The computer has no sound card or board sound. See [Sound cards](jsc:sound_cards).
jsc.guide.frames_settings.fix5: The computer cannot play a sound at the moment, so Test is off.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.problem1: A page says "Coming in a future update".
jsc.guide.frames_settings.problem2: The button "Restart to firmware" is missing.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.problem3: The Sound page says "No speakers linked".
jsc.guide.frames_settings.problem4: The Sound page says "No sound hardware".
jsc.guide.frames_settings.problem5: The Test button on the Sound page is grey.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.step1: Open Settings from the Start menu. On Frames 7, open Control Panel.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.step2: Click a page in the list at the left, or a category or tile on the home page.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.step3: Change the setting you want on that page.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.table1_1_2: Choose the wallpaper and the clock, and on some editions the accent, the theme and the light or dark look.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.table1_2_2: Name the computer, read its hardware, and restart into the firmware.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.table1_3_2: See the link of the computer, share folders, and allow or refuse remote programs.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.table1_4_2: See each disk and its size. The system disk is marked.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.table1_5_2: Set the brightness, and the scale of the screen in percent.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.table1_6_2: See the installed programs, and uninstall them.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.table1_7_2: Set the volume, mute the sound, choose the output, and test the sound.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.table1_8_2: Not built yet. The page says "Coming in a future update".
jsc.guide.frames_settings.table2: The categories of the Control Panel
jsc.guide.frames_settings.table2_2_3: Users, which is not built yet
jsc.guide.frames_settings.table2_5_3: Sound, through its title; Display, through its line of text
jsc.guide.frames_settings.text1: Settings is where you change how your Frames works: its look, its sound, its network and its disks. It has a left column that lists its pages, and the page you choose appears at the right. On Frames 95, Frames XP, Frames 10 and Frames 11 the program is called Settings. On Frames 7 the same program is called Control Panel.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.text10: On Frames 7, the page also shows the [experience rating](jsc:effects), which is a set of scores for the parts. The button "Restart to firmware" restarts the computer into its [firmware](jsc:firmware) setup.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.text2: Frames 7 and Frames 10 open Settings on a home page. On Frames 7 the home page is a list of categories, and on Frames 10 it is a grid of tiles. The other editions open on their first page.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.text3: The page [Personalize](jsc:personalize) is explained on its own page, and so is the Effects page, reached from several of these pages.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.text4: Frames 95 lists its eight pages at the left, with no home page. Its [effects page](jsc:effects) is reached from Display.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.text5: Frames XP lists the same eight pages. Its Effects page, called Performance Options, is reached from System.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.text6: Frames 10 opens on a home page: the heading "Frames Settings", and eight tiles in two rows of four. The tiles are System, Display, Sound, Network, Personalize, Storage, Programs and Users.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.text7: Frames 11 lists the same eight pages, with no home page. Its Effects page, called Visual effects, is reached from Personalize.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.text8: The Control Panel of Frames 7 has seven categories. Each one is a link, with a line of text under its name.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.text9: The System page has a box for the name of the computer. It shows "(unnamed)" while the name is empty. Below it are the facts of the hardware: the processor and its speed in megahertz (MHz), the architecture, the memory in megabytes (MB), the graphics memory, the system and the platform.
jsc.guide.frames_settings.title: Settings and the Control Panel
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.fix1: The stick is not in a Dock Station, or the Dock Station is not joined to the computer. Plug the stick in, and join the Dock Station ([](jsc:peripheral_cables)).
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.fix2: Choose another disk with room, or erase this disk as described in the Frames 95 section ([](jsc:frames_setup_95_xp)).
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.fix3: Put the stick back in the Dock Station, start the setup again, and leave the stick in until the copy ends.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.problem1: The firmware does not offer the installer, and says: "No installation medium is in a drive linked to this machine."
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.problem2: The disk page says: "No room here. Erase this disk, or choose another."
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.problem3: The copy stops and says: "The medium was taken out before the system was written."
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.step1: Put the Frames 7 DVD in a DVD Drive that is joined to the computer.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.step2: Turn the computer on, and choose "Frames 7 installer" in the firmware.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.step3: Follow the pages in the table below, in the order the table gives them.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.step4: Plug the stick into the USB port of a Dock Station that is joined to the computer.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.step5: Turn the computer on, and choose "Frames 10 installer" or "Frames 11 installer" in the firmware.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.step6: Follow the pages of your edition, as the tables above show them.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.table1_2_: "Where do you want to install Frames?"
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.table1_3_: "Installing Frames...", with the steps Copying Frames files, Expanding Frames files, Installing features, Installing updates and Completing installation.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.table1_4_: "Choose a name for your computer to distinguish it on the network."
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.table2_2_: "Where do you want to install Frames?"
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.table2_3_: "Installing Frames", with the steps Copying Frames files, Getting files ready for installation, Installing features, Installing updates and Finishing up.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.table2_4_: "Who's going to use this PC?" The answer becomes the computer's name.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.table3_1_: One large "Install now" button, which asks nothing.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.table3_2_: "Where do you want to install Frames 11?"
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.table3_4_: "Installing Frames 11", with the steps Copying files, Creating the system folders, Adding the built-in programs and Setting up the boot entry.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.table3_5_: "Setup is finished." The button on this card is Restart.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.text1: Frames 7 comes on a DVD, which you read in a DVD Drive. Frames 10 and Frames 11 come on a USB stick, which you plug into a Dock Station joined to the computer ([](jsc:dock_station)).
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.text2: Each of the three has its own setup window, in the look of its era. They ask for the same things, a disk, a name and a copy, but in a different order and with different words.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.text3: On Frames 7, the setup is a glass window titled "Install Frames". Its welcome page has one large "Install now" button.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.text4: Frames 10 has its own look, titled "Frames Setup". Its name page takes the whole screen.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.text5: Frames 11 uses cards, in a window titled "Frames 11 Setup". Each card has its own buttons: Next and Back, and Erase disk on the disk page. The welcome card asks nothing: it has one button, Install now.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.text6: The USB stick holds the system for Frames 10 and 11. It does not go into the computer: it goes into the USB port of a Dock Station, and the Dock Station must be joined to the computer. The stick's tooltip says "Plug into a linked Dock Station", and a hint says to run the setup program or to install from This PC.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_7_10_11.title: Setting up Frames 7, 10 and 11
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.definition1: The installer program that copies a system onto a disk.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.fix1: Erase a disk you no longer need, or add a bigger disk ([](jsc:disks)).
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.fix2: Choose another disk from the list, or erase this one if its files are not needed.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.fix3: Put the CD in a CD Drive that is joined to the computer ([](jsc:peripheral_cables)).
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.fix4: Put the CD back in the drive and start the setup again. Leave the CD in until the copy is done.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.problem1: The screen says: "No disk in this machine has room for it."
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.problem2: The screen says: "No room here. Erase this disk, or choose another."
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.problem3: The firmware does not offer the installer, and says: "No installation medium is in a drive linked to this machine."
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.problem4: The copy stops and says: "The medium was taken out before the system was written."
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.step1: Put the Frames 95 CD in a CD Drive that is joined to the computer.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.step2: Turn the computer on, and choose "Frames 95 installer" in the firmware.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.step3: Read the check on the first page, then press [[Enter]] to continue, or [[F3]] to exit.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.step4: Choose the disk for the system, then go on to the next page.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.step5: Type the computer's name, then go on.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.step6: Wait while the files are copied.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.step7: When the last page says "Setup is finished.", the copy is done.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.step8: You can then take the CD out of the drive.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.table1_1_2: The check: Generation, Processor, Memory, the disk and the installation medium, each with its answer.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.table1_2_2: "Choose a Disk", with the disks of the machine.

jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.text1: Frames 95 and Frames XP both come on a CD, so you need a CD Drive joined to the computer ([](jsc:drives)). The disc holds the setup program, SETUP.EXE, which copies the system onto a disk. Frames 95 and XP each have their own setup pages, and the keys below matter on the Frames XP disk page.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.text2: The firmware offers the disc as "Frames 95 installer", and choosing it starts the setup ([](jsc:firmware)).
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.text3: Frames XP comes on the same CD and starts the same way: choose "Frames XP installer" in the firmware. Its pages are different, and its disk page lists the keys you need.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.text4: Both setups use the same rules for the disk. The setup proposes the first disk with room for the system. A disk has room when its free space is at least the system's footprint.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.text5: If the chosen disk is too small, the setup says "No room here. Erase this disk, or choose another." Erasing is asked twice: the first answer only asks, and the second erases the disk. The question reads "Erase Disk" with the disk's number. The erase happens before the copy, and choosing another disk before the copy starts cancels it.
jsc.guide.frames_setup_95_xp.title: Setting up Frames 95 and XP
jsc.guide.frames_which_machine.definitio: One version of Frames, with its own installer and its own desktop.
The disc or stick a system is installed from, such as a CD or a USB stick.
The program on the motherboard that starts the computer and tests its hardware before it hands over to a system.
The memory the running system keeps for itself before any program opens, in megabytes.
The space a system takes on its disk, in megabytes. The disk counts it in items.
jsc.guide.frames_which_machine.fix1: Choose the edition for this machine's era, or use a newer machine ([](jsc:eras)).
jsc.guide.frames_which_machine.fix2: Install a disk in the machine first, then start the installer again ([](jsc:disks)).
jsc.guide.frames_which_machine.fix3: Choose a bigger disk, or another disk with room ([](jsc:disks)).
jsc.guide.frames_which_machine.problem1: The screen says: "Frames 10 needs Standard era hardware or newer; this machine is Legacy era."
jsc.guide.frames_which_machine.problem2: The screen says: "No disk is installed to put Frames 7 on."
jsc.guide.frames_which_machine.problem3: The screen says: "The target disk has no room for", then the system's name and, in brackets, the megabytes it needs.

jsc.guide.frames_which_machine.table2: Own RAM and footprint of each edition
