jsc.guide.sigma_example_old_names.table2: Old names for numbers and text
jsc.guide.sigma_example_old_names.table4: A percent sign, written as itself.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_old_names.text1: Old names are short, familiar functions, such as printf, puts and strlen, that older programs use. Each one is a short form of a call the library already has. For example, puts gives the same result as Console.PrintLine.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_old_names.text2: A method or a variable of your own program with the same name wins. The program calls its own method, not the old name. This program needs version 2, because it uses old names that version 2 adds, and its Main takes arguments.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_old_names.text3: The text of a printf format holds holes, and a value fills each hole. A hole is a percent sign and a letter, and a number written into the hole sets its width.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_old_names.title: Old names
jsc.guide.sigma_example_programs.definit: A number a program hands back when it ends. 0 usually means success.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_programs.fix1: Use Wait with a time, which answers false when the time is up.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_programs.fix2: Build the program in Sigma#, the full language.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_programs.heading: The program
What the lines do
jsc.guide.sigma_example_programs.problem: The program waits, and it does not go on, because the process has not ended.
The Sigma compiler refuses Thread, because these machines run one thing at a time.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_programs.table1_: Gives back the lines the process printed.
Sends the text hello to the process with that number.
Starts a thread: a body of code that runs beside the program, taking turns with it.
Pause the thread for a short time, or let the other code take a turn.
The thread that runs this code, the number of the worker, and whether it runs.
Wait for the thread to end, wait for a time, or stop the thread.
Ends the program and hands 0 back to the machine as its exit code.
Names this program, so the process list shows the name. It costs nothing.
Read the program's name, its arguments, the number of events lost, and its own process.
Starts a program at a path, with no arguments, with a list of arguments, or with a list and a third text.
Runs one line at this machine's own prompt, to the end, and gives back what it printed.
Asks to be called with each message, and the lambda prints the message.
The number, the name and the computer of another process.
Tell whether the process still runs, and the number it gave back when it ended.
Wait until the process ends, or wait up to a time and answer whether it ended.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_programs.text1: A program can start other programs, talk to them and wait for them. This example names itself, starts three programs, sends one of them a message, waits for two of them, stops the third, and runs a thread beside itself.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_programs.text2: A process is a program that runs on the machine and is listed in its process list. Starting one costs more than most calls, because the machine makes a whole process ([](jsc:sigma_running)). If you start a process, you can wait for it, or leave it running.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_programs.title: Programs
jsc.guide.sigma_example_redstone.definit: A block that links the machine to the redstone of the world, so a program can read or emit a signal.
The power of a redstone signal, from 0 to 15: strength 0 is off, and strength 15 is the strongest.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_redstone.fix1: Give the interface that name, and test for null before you use it.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_redstone.fix3: Link the interface to the machine again.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_redstone.heading: The program
What the lines do
jsc.guide.sigma_example_redstone.problem: No interface has the name, so the value is null.
Out is given a number outside 0 to 15, and the program stops with "16 is not a redstone strength, which runs from 0 to 15".
The interface is no longer linked to the machine, and the program stops with "no Redstone Interface named 'Gate' is linked to this machine".
jsc.guide.sigma_example_redstone.table1_: Finds the Redstone Interface called Gate. It gives null when none is linked under that name.
Makes the interface read the signal.
Makes the interface emit strength 15, the strongest.
The strength the interface reads or emits. It is 0 when nothing powers it.
Finds a second interface by its name, in the same way.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_redstone.text1: Redstone is the power signal of the world, with a strength from 0 to 15. A Redstone Interface links the machine to the redstone of the world, so a program can read a signal or emit one ([](jsc:redstone_interfaces)).
jsc.guide.sigma_example_redstone.text2: This example finds an interface called Gate, sets it to read and to emit strength 15, and prints its name and its strength. You can match each line with the table below. It then finds an interface called Lever and prints its name.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_redstone.title: Redstone
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.definition: A plain tone at one pitch, for a set time.
How high a sound is, measured in hertz. 440 hertz is the note A4.
A named pitch, such as C4, that a tune can play.
Several notes played together, written with plus signs, such as C4+E4+G4.
A block that makes sound for the machine.
A music file on the machine's disk, such as an .ogg or a .wav file.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.fix1: Check that the machine has a sound device and that its volume is above 0.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.fix2: Write notes such as C4, a pitch in hertz, or R for a rest.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.fix3: Play the tune through the sound card, which plays the whole chord.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.fix4: Test for null before you use the speaker, and check its name.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.fix5: Check the path, written with slashes, and the kind of the file.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.fix6: A beep is set to the nearest limit, so give a pitch from 20 to 20,000 hertz.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.problem1: Tones answers false, and no tune plays.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.problem2: A tune holds a word that is not a note, and the program stops with a message that ends "is not a note".
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.problem3: A chord on the speaker inside the case sounds as its first note only.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.problem4: Speaker.Named gives null, because no speaker has that name.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.problem5: Play answers false for a file that is missing or cannot be played.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.problem6: A beep asks for a pitch below 20 or above 20,000 hertz.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.table1_1_2: Plays a beep at 880 hertz for 200 milliseconds.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.table1_2_2: Plays a tune: C4 for 250 milliseconds, then E4 and G4, then the chord C4, E4 and G4 for 500 milliseconds. It answers true when the tune plays.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.table1_3_2: Plays a recording from the machine's disks. It answers false when the file is not playable.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.table1_4_2: Stops the sound of the program.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.table1_5_2: Finds a speaker linked to the machine by its name. It gives null when none has that name.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.table1_6_2: Plays a recording through that speaker only, and answers true when it plays.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.text1: Sound makes a beep or a tune through the machine, and plays a recording from its disks. This example uses the four sound calls, and one speaker found by its name.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.text2: A beep comes out of the speaker inside the case, and each new beep cuts off the one before it. A tune plays through the sound card, which plays every note of a chord.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.text3: A recording from the machine's disks comes out of the monitors and speakers, as its system says.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_sound.title: Sound
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.definition: Adding one to a value, written ++.
Taking one from a value, written --.
An operator written before a name, such as ++count, which gives the new value.
An operator written after a name, such as count++, which gives the old value.
An assignment that does an operation on the variable first, such as total += 2, which means total = total + 2.
A variable around a lambda that the lambda keeps and can change.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.fix1: Give the variable a value of its own type, such as a whole number for an int.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.fix2: Write a comparison that gives true or false, such as count > 0.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.fix3: Put an assignment, a call or an increment on the line, or store the value in a variable.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.fix4: Assign only to a variable, a field, a property or an element.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.fix5: Add using System.Collections.*; at the top of the file, as the example does.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.problem1: A value of one type is stored in a variable of another, and the compiler says "cannot convert" with code S3003.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.problem2: A condition is not a bool, such as a number in an if, and the compiler refuses it with code S3009.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.problem3: A line holds only a value, such as 5;, and the compiler refuses it with code S2006.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.problem4: An assignment goes to something that is not a variable, a field, a property or an element, with code S2008.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.problem5: A name such as List is not found, and the compiler asks for a using line, with code S3040.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_10_: Change a variable that the lambda keeps from the lines around it.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_11_: Each compound assignment does its operation on combined and stores the result.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_12_: Adds the number to the end of the text.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_13_: An assignment gives back the value it stored, so answered gets the new value.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_14_: Sets local to 7, and stores 7 in plain as well.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_1_2: Change a local variable by one, up and down, with the operator before and after the name.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_2_2: Stores the old value in before, and then adds one to local.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_3_2: Adds one to local first, and then stores the new value in after.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_4_2: Change a long, a float and a double by one.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_5_2: Change a static field of the program and a static field of a class.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_6_2: Changes a field of an object.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_7_2: Changes an element of an array.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_8_2: Changes an element of a list.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.table1_9_2: Changes the value stored under the key a in a map.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.text1: A step changes a variable by one, or by an amount you give. An increment adds one, a decrement takes one, and a compound assignment does an operation on the variable and stores the result.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.text2: You write ++ or -- before or after a name. Before the name, you get the new value. After the name, you get the old value. The example shows both for each kind of place you can change.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_steps.title: Steps
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.definitio: A type whose values are copied when they are stored or handed over, such as a struct.
A type whose values are one shared object: every name for it sees the same object, as with a class.
Belongs to the type, not to one object: every part of the program sees the same value.
A row of values of one type with a fixed length, made with new and the length, such as new Vec[3].
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.fix1: A struct can implement interfaces, but it cannot have a base class. Remove the base class from the struct.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.problem1: A struct declares a base class, and the compiler refuses it with code S3041.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.table1_1_: Declares Vec, a struct with two fields, X and Y, both of type int.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.table1_2_: Declares a class with a struct field called Spot and a static field called Origin.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.table1_3_: Stores a copy of one in copy. Changing the copy leaves one as it was.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.table1_4_: Each store makes its own copy, so the three places hold separate values.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.table1_5_: Hands one to a method, which gives back a copy of it.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.table1_6_: Stores a copy in an element of the array.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.table1_7_: Adds a copy to the list.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.table1_8_: Loops over the array and the list, and reads each struct in turn.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.text1: A struct is a value. When you store one, or hand it to a method, you get a copy of it. This example shows that with a struct called Vec, and it puts the struct into a field, a static field, an array and a list.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.text2: A class is a reference type: two names can point at one object, and both see every change made to it. The class Held in this example holds a struct in a field, and its static field is shared by the whole program.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.text3: A field you did not give a value starts as an empty struct, so a struct field is never nothing. An array of structs works the same way: new Vec[3] makes three empty ones.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_values.title: Values
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.definiti: Something that happens, such as a click or a change, which a method can answer.
A widget that a mod adds, identified by its own id, such as mod:name.
The name of an item in the game, such as minecraft:diamond.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.fix1: Run the program on a machine that draws its windows, not only its terminal.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.fix2: Put fewer widgets in the window, and count the ones inside rows and columns.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.fix3: Use at most 8 columns in a table.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.fix4: Keep each menu to 64 entries or fewer.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.fix5: Keep each list to 1024 rows or fewer.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.problem1: A picture, a chart, an item slot or a component is made on a machine with only its terminal, and the program stops.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.problem2: A window holds more than 256 widgets, and the program stops with "a window holds at most 256 widgets, counting the ones inside rows and columns".
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.problem3: A table gets more than 8 columns, and the program stops with "a table has at most 8 columns".
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.problem4: A menu gets more than 64 entries, and the program stops with "a menu holds at most 64 entries".
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.problem5: A list gets more than 1024 rows, and the program stops with "a list holds at most 1024 rows".
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.table1_1: A bar of menus with entries. Picked and PickedMenu tell what the player picked.
A menu that opens on its widget when the player clicks it with the other button.
A line of text, with a few sections at its right.
A picture read from the machine's disk, as the paint program saves it.
A line drawn through the numbers added to it, between a least and a most.
Lines one under another, the newest at the bottom. A line with WARN or ERROR is picked out.
A dialog in which the player chooses a file. Show opens it on a window.
One slot that holds an item, shown by its item id and how many.
A grid of items with a search line above it. The player picks one.
Shows an Operation: its text, its state, how much is done, and its computer.
A box for several lines of text. OnChange runs when its text changes.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.table1_2: A widget that a mod adds, named by an id such as corpus:dial. OnAction runs when it acts.
A whole number between a least and a most, moved a step at a time.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.table1_3: A set of choices, one of which is picked. Selected is the picked choice, counted from 1, and 0 for none.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.table1_4: A box with a list of choices. Selected is the picked choice.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.table1_5: A box with a caption, and a widget inside it.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.table1_6: Tabs, each with a title and a widget. The first one added shows first.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.table1_7: Shows a widget that is taller than its room, and the player scrolls it.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.table1_8: Rows and columns of text. Cell gives the text in one cell. A table holds at most 8 columns.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.table1_9: A tree of text. Add gives back the number of the new node, and NodeText gives its text.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.text1: This example shows the rest of the widgets: text areas and number boxes, choices, tabs, tables, trees, menus, status bars, pictures, charts, logs, file dialogs, item slots, operations and components that a mod adds.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.text2: Some widgets draw pictures, charts, items or components. A machine with only its terminal cannot draw them, so making one there stops the program, and the message says so.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.text3: The handler is a method that you write and name on the widget.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.text4: Widgets have events such as OnChange, OnSelect and OnClick. Each one names the method called when the player acts.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_widgets.title: Widgets
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.definiti: A box on the desktop, with a title and widgets inside it.
A box that lines up its widgets across, one after another.
A box that lines up its widgets down, one under another.
A number that gives a widget a share of the room left over. Only widgets with a weight share that room.
A blank area that a program draws on, with shapes, lines and text.
A method that the program names, and that is called when something happens.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.fix1: Put fewer widgets in the window. Widgets inside rows and columns count too, so remove some of those as well.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.fix2: Split the widgets between two rows or two columns.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.fix3: Put each widget in one place only, and never inside itself.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.fix4: Draw fewer shapes, or use a second canvas for the rest.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.problem1: A window holds more than 256 widgets, counting the ones inside rows and columns, and the program stops with "a window holds at most 256 widgets, counting the ones inside rows and columns".
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.problem2: A row or a column holds more than 256 widgets, and the program stops with "a row or a column holds at most 256 widgets".
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.problem3: A widget is put inside itself, and the program stops with "a widget cannot hold itself or a widget it is inside".
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.problem4: A canvas gets more than 4,096 strokes, and the program stops with "a canvas holds at most 4096 strokes".
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.table1_1: Draw a text or one point. ClickX and ClickY give where the player last clicked.
Adds the label with a weight of 1, which takes a share of the room left over.
Makes the column the main content of the window.
Places the button at position 0, 0, with a width of 20 and a height of 10.
Names the method called when the window closes.
Opens the window on the desktop and its taskbar. The window stays open after the tick that opened it.
Open says whether the window is open. Close closes it.
Shows a small box with a title and a line of text.
Makes a window with the title Corpus, a width of 240 and a height of 150.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.table1_2: A row lines its widgets up across, and a column lines them up down. Spacing sets the room between them.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.table1_3: A label shows a text. Its size is set by Width and Height.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.table1_4: A button with a text on it. OnClick names the method called when the player clicks it.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.table1_5: A box to type in. OnChange runs when its text changes, and OnSubmit when the player submits it.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.table1_6: A tick box with a text. Checked says whether it is ticked.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.table1_7: A bar that shows a value between a least and a most.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.table1_8: A list of lines. Selected is the chosen line, and OnSelect runs when one is picked.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.table1_9: A blank area to draw on, 100 wide and 50 high. Each drawing call paints one shape or text in a colour from 0 to 15.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.text1: A window is a box on the desktop, with a title. This example builds a window, puts a row and a column of widgets in it, and shows it. A widget is a piece of a window, such as a label, a button or a box to type in. You make a window with a title, a width and a height.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.text2: The machine's own system draws the widgets, so the same program looks like the system it runs under. The example closes its window near the end of Main, and then shows a message box.
jsc.guide.sigma_example_windows.title: Windows
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.definitio: A numbered stage of Sigma#. A later stage adds names, and a program that uses one of them needs that stage.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.fix1: Fix the first error it prints, then build the file again. A file with an error gets no .asm file.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.fix3: Build with the version the name needs, or take the name out of the program.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.fix4: Add the using line it asks for above the namespace line, then build again.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.problem1: The compiler prints an error and says nothing was written.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.problem2: The message reads "'abc' is not a version of Σ#; there are 1 to 2", because the text after --lang is not a version.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.problem3: The compiler refuses a name that the chosen version does not have, with code S3057.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.problem4: The compiler says a name is in a namespace and asks for a using line, with code S3040.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.step1: Save the program as a file that ends in .sgs, such as Buses.sgs.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.step2: Type sgsc Buses.sgs at the prompt and press [[Enter]].
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.step3: Read the answer. When it says wrote Buses.asm, the program is built.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.step4: Type sigma run Buses.asm and press [[Enter]] to start the program.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.table1_1_: Names the built file, in place of the source's name with .asm.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.table1_2_: Chooses the instruction set. Without it, the default jsc:x86 is used.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.table1_3_: Chooses the language version the program is checked against: 1 or 2.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.text1: Every example in this chapter is a whole program in Sigma#, the full language. Each one is a single file, and you can type it in, build it and run it on a computer of the mod.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.text2: An example starts with using lines, which bring the library's names into the file. Its class has a method called Main, and the program starts there ([](jsc:sigma_entry_points)).
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.text3: The compiler writes the built program beside the source file, with the ending .asm. After a good build it prints wrote Buses.asm, then a line that begins run it with: sigma run Buses.asm. The compiler is explained in ([](jsc:sigma_compile)).
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.text4: The version decides which names a program may use. A program that uses a name from version 2 needs version 2. The table below gives the version each example needs.
jsc.guide.sigma_examples_intro.title: Running the examples
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.definition: The text file in a project folder that names the project and lists its source files and settings.
The method where a console program starts.
The interface a script implements, with the methods the runtime calls on it: OnInit, OnTick and OnDestroy.
A line at the top of a source file that brings a library into the program.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.fix1: Keep one class with a static Main, or one class that implements IScript, and remove the others.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.fix2: Read the error and fix the line it names, then build again ([](jsc:sigma_errors)).
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.heading1: Your first run in Virtual Studio
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.problem1: "a program needs exactly one place to start" appears, with the count of starts it found.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.problem2: The build prints an error that names a file and a place in it, such as hello.sgs(3,5): line 3, fifth character.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.step1: Open the New Project wizard with [[Ctrl]]+[[Shift]]+[[N]] in Virtual Studio.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.step2: Choose the Console App offer for Sigma#, and type a name, such as Hello.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.step3: Press [[F5]] to build the project and run it.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.step4: Read the line the program prints in the terminal.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.table1_1_2: A program with a Main that runs at the terminal it was started from, prints as it goes, and is gone when it returns.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.table1_2_2: A program that stays up. It is set up once, it is called again and again while it runs, and it is told when it is stopped.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.table1_3_2: Classes that other projects share. It has no start of its own, and it compiles into the projects that use it.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.table1_4_2: A project with no files in it, for starting from nothing.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.text1: A program starts in one place, and the compiler must find that place. The simplest program prints one line and ends. On Frames, Virtual Studio can make a starter project for it with its wizard, and then one key runs it ([](jsc:virtual_studio)).
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.text2: The wizard offers four kinds of project, and each comes in both languages. You pick the kind and the language, then give the project a name.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.text3: The name may use only letters, digits and underscores, and it must not start with a digit. The name becomes the [namespace](jsc:sigma_namespaces_using), the class name, and the text the program prints.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.text4: The wizard writes the project file, NAME.sgsproj for Sigma# (NAME.sgproj for Sigma), and the source file, NAME.sgs for Sigma# (NAME.sg for Sigma). When you build, the listing goes to build/NAME.asm.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.text5: Here is the starter code of a Sigma# console app, in a project called Hello. The name Hello is used for the namespace, for the class, and for the text the program prints.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.text6: The same program in Sigma looks like this. Sigma prints with printf, and you end the text with a line break yourself, written as a backslash and an n.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.text7: A program needs exactly one place to start: a class that implements IScript, or a class with a static Main. A Main is static, returns void or int, and takes nothing or the arguments as a string array. Each using line brings a library into the program, so its names can be written short.
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.text8: Returning an int from Main, or taking the arguments, needs Sigma# version 2. Each project holds its own version ([](jsc:sigma_projects)).
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.text9: The program prints Hello from Hello, and it is gone when Main returns. Compiling it on the command line is shown in [](jsc:sigma_compile).
jsc.guide.sigma_first_program.title: Your first program
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.definition1: A way for a class to take on the members of another class, and then add to them or replace some of them.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.definition2: Marks a method that a derived class may replace.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.definition3: Marks a method that replaces a virtual method of the base class.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.definition4: Marks a method with no body, or a class that cannot be made with new, which needs a derived class to finish it.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.fix1: Name a class as the base class. Interfaces after the colon are Sigma# only.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.fix2: Add override in front of the method.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.fix3: Add virtual to the method in the base class.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.fix4: Remove override, or check that the name and the parameters match the method above.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.fix5: In Sigma#, declare the class abstract, or give the method a body.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.fix6: Make an object of a class that derives from it, and give that class the bodies it needs.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.problem1: The compiler says only a class or an interface can stand behind the colon.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.problem2: The compiler says 'Name' is already on 'Vehicle', so write it with override to replace it.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.problem3: The compiler says 'Name' on 'Vehicle' is not virtual, so nothing can replace it.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.problem4: The compiler says 'Name' is written with override but nothing above it has it.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.problem5: The compiler says 'Draw' has no body, so 'Shape' has to be declared abstract.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.problem6: The compiler says 'Shape' is abstract, so it cannot be made with new.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.text1: Inheritance lets one class build on another. A class that inherits from a base class has all of the base class's members, and it can add new ones or replace some of them. You write the base class after a colon, as in class Car : Vehicle. A class has one base class at most.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.text2: A method that a derived class may replace must be marked virtual in the base class. The derived class replaces it with override, and keeps the same parameters. Without override, a method with the same name and parameters as one above it is refused, so a method never gets hidden by accident.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.text3: An abstract method has no body. It says that each class deriving from this one must write one. A method marked abstract needs an abstract class, and an abstract class cannot be made with new. Sigma has virtual and override, but no abstract classes and no abstract methods. Its compiler refuses them and suggests a class with virtual methods that do nothing.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.text4: To call the version of a method that you replaced, write base.Name(args). It calls the version in the base class. A struct cannot have a base class, and a static method cannot be virtual, override or abstract.
jsc.guide.sigma_inheritance.title: Inheritance: virtual, override and abstract
jsc.guide.sigma_install_community.fix1: Install the program from the install media of the system instead ([](jsc:installing)).
jsc.guide.sigma_install_community.fix2: Ask the player who published it to publish it again from a built file.
jsc.guide.sigma_install_community.fix3: Install the Sigma runtime on this computer ([](jsc:sigma_installing)), then install again.
jsc.guide.sigma_install_community.fix4: Put a system disk in the computer, then install again.
jsc.guide.sigma_install_community.fix5: Check the system disk, then install again.
jsc.guide.sigma_install_community.proble: The install says this system installs programs from install media, not a package manager.
The install says the Mirror's copy of this package is not readable.
The install says mypkg is a Σ# program; install sigma first.
The install says no system disk to install onto.

jsc.guide.sigma_install_community.step1: Type the install command of your package manager, with the package's name.
jsc.guide.sigma_install_community.step2: Open the program from the desktop.
jsc.guide.sigma_install_community.text1: Players can publish packages for anyone on the network. You install one like any other program: with the install command of your system's package manager and the package's name, such as apt install mypkg on a Debian or Ubuntu system ([](jsc:software_commands)).
jsc.guide.sigma_install_community.text2: Installing a player's package needs the Sigma runtime on your computer ([](jsc:sigma_installing)). Without it, the install stops and says to install sigma first.
jsc.guide.sigma_install_community.text3: The game unpacks each package into a folder of its own: PROGRAMS, then the package's name. The folder holds only that package's files, so two packages cannot overwrite each other. The package then shows on the desktop with its icon, and opening it runs the program.
jsc.guide.sigma_install_community.text4: To remove a package, type the remove command of your package manager, with its name, such as apt remove mypkg. The game deletes exactly the files the install wrote, then the folder, and answers removed mypkg.
jsc.guide.sigma_install_community.title: Installing a package other players published
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.definition1: The package scc, which turns your Sigma source into a listing.
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.definition2: The package sgsc, which turns your Sigma# source into a listing.
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.definition3: The package sigma, which runs your listings on the computer.
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.definition4: The line where you type a command, and where the system answers it.
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.definition5: A command word the system knows, such as install or run.
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.fix1: Install the Sigma compiler, scc, on this Vintage computer. Or use a Legacy computer or later.
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.fix2: The Mirror does not offer the package to this computer. Check that a Mainframe runs the Mirror. On Frames, search for the name with pckmgr search.
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.fix3: Connect this computer to a network whose Mainframe runs the Mirror service.
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.fix4: Use Frames, Linux or FreeBSD for this package, since they have a package manager.
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.fix5: The computer lacks the era or the free disk space the package needs. Free some disk space, or use a computer of a newer era.
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.fix6: Type the name of the package after install, for example pckmgr install scc.

jsc.guide.sigma_installing.problem3: "could not resolve mirror:// - connect this computer to a network whose Mainframe runs the Mirror service" appears.

jsc.guide.sigma_installing.step3: Type pckmgr install sgsc and press [[Enter]].
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.step4: Type pckmgr install sigma and press [[Enter]].

jsc.guide.sigma_installing.text1: Sigma and Sigma# do not come with the computer. You install three packages: the Σ Compiler (scc), the Σ# Compiler (sgsc) and the Sigma Runtime (sigma). A package is installed by its name, the way every program is ([](jsc:programs)).
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.text2: The Sigma compiler is the smallest of the three. It is the only one a Vintage computer can hold, because the Sigma# compiler and the runtime need a Legacy computer or later.
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.text3: On Frames, the edition matters too. Frames 95 can install the Sigma compiler only: the Sigma# compiler and the runtime need Frames XP or later.
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.text4: The packages come from the Mirror, the network's package repository. It is a service on a Standard Mainframe, so your computer must be on a network whose Mainframe runs the Mirror ([](jsc:mirror)).
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.text5: The name is the package's own name, such as scc or sgsc. On MC-DOS, MC-NET and UNIX System V, programs install from install media only, not from the Mirror ([](jsc:programs)).
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.text6: Once a package is installed, its command appears at the prompt. The prompt is the line where you type a command, and the system answers there. Each command word is a verb: a word the system knows, such as install or run.
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.text7: Until a package is installed, its verbs do not exist at the prompt. The runtime adds the sigma verb, and the packaging tool sgpack comes with it ([](jsc:sigma_sharing)).
jsc.guide.sigma_installing.title: Installing the compilers and the runtime
jsc.guide.sigma_interfaces_records.fix1: Write every method the interface lists, as a public method.
jsc.guide.sigma_interfaces_records.fix2: In Sigma, write a class whose methods are virtual, and derive from it, as the Sigma page on inheritance shows.
jsc.guide.sigma_interfaces_records.fix3: In Sigma, write a struct with the same fields, or use Sigma# for a record.
jsc.guide.sigma_interfaces_records.probl: The compiler says 'Square' says it is a 'IShape' but does not have 'Area'.
Sigma refuses the word interface and suggests a class with virtual methods.
Sigma refuses the word record and suggests a struct with the same fields.
jsc.guide.sigma_interfaces_records.table: Method signatures only, with no fields.
Not applicable: it holds no values.
readonly fields, set by the constructor.
No: it is shared, as every class is.
jsc.guide.sigma_interfaces_records.text1: This page describes Sigma#. Sigma has neither interfaces nor records. Its compiler refuses the word interface and suggests a class with virtual methods instead, and it refuses the word record and suggests a struct with the same fields.
jsc.guide.sigma_interfaces_records.text2: An interface lists the methods that a class must write. It holds method signatures only: a result type, a name and parameters, ending in a semicolon, with no body. A class says that it writes an interface with a colon, and then writes every method of it as a public method. An interface can stand behind another interface after a colon too.
jsc.guide.sigma_interfaces_records.text3: IScript is a built-in interface that makes a program stay up. The [entry points page](jsc:sigma_entry_points) explains it.
jsc.guide.sigma_interfaces_records.text4: A record is a class-like type made of readonly fields. You write its fields in brackets after its name. record Point(int X, int Y); declares a Point with two fields, X and Y. Each field is public and readonly, and the record gets one constructor that takes the fields in order. The record also writes ToString for you, which prints its fields by name. Two records with the same fields are equal, because a record is compared by its values.
jsc.guide.sigma_interfaces_records.title: Interfaces and records
jsc.guide.sigma_limits.definition1: The memory a running program holds for the objects it makes, such as text and lists. Its size is the memory the program was given.
jsc.guide.sigma_limits.fix1: Close a program or a window, add memory to the computer ([Memory](jsc:memory)), or start the program with a smaller --heap.
jsc.guide.sigma_limits.fix2: The program holds too much at once. Make it hold less, or give it more with --heap, up to 64 MB.
jsc.guide.sigma_limits.fix3: A console keeps 200 lines or 64,000 characters. Print less, or read the output sooner.
jsc.guide.sigma_limits.fix4: Close one of the windows before you open another.
jsc.guide.sigma_limits.fix5: The time allowed per tick is used up. Raise the balance keys in jstech-balance.toml, if the server can spare the time.

jsc.guide.sigma_limits.text1: A running program has limits. They stop one program from taking all of a computer's memory or all of its time. Most limits are fixed. Two of the time limits can be changed in the config file jstech-balance.toml.
jsc.guide.sigma_limits.text2: Memory is the first limit. Each program has a heap: the memory it holds for the objects it makes, such as text and lists. Every object counts against the memory the program was given. Without --heap, a program gets 1 MB. The most you can give it is 64 MB.
jsc.guide.sigma_limits.text3: The config file jstech-balance.toml holds two keys: balance.program_machine_micros, for one computer, and balance.program_server_micros, for all the computers together. Both are times in microseconds.
jsc.guide.sigma_limits.title: The limits of a running program
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.definition1: The part of a pair that finds its value in a map, such as the name of a fruit.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.definition2: A collection of pairs: each key leads to one value. Written Map<K, V> in Sigma#.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.fix1: The index must run from 0 up to one less than Count. Check it before you read the item.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.fix2: Use the indexes from 0 up to the length minus one.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.fix3: Walk Keys() or Values() instead, as in foreach (string name in count.Keys()).
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.fix4: Use an array, with a count of your own beside it, as Sigma allows.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.problem1: The program stops and says "there is no place 3 in a list of 3".
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.problem2: The program stops and says "there is no place 4 in an array of 4".
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.problem3: The compiler says foreach walks an array or a list, not a Map.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.problem4: The compiler refuses List in Sigma, and says to use an array, and a count of your own beside it.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table1_1_3: How many items the list holds.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table1_2_3: Puts the item at the end.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table1_3_3: Puts the item in the place index, moving the later items along.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table1_4_3: Takes away the item at the place index.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table1_5_3: Takes away an item that matches, and tells whether it found one.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table1_7_3: Whether the item is in the list.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table1_8_3: The place of the item, or -1 when it is not there.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table1_9_3: Reads or changes the item at the place index.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table2_1_3: How many pairs the map holds.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table2_2_3: Adds the pair, or changes the value of a key that is already there.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table2_3_3: The value of the key. A missing key gives back null and does not stop the program.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table2_4_3: Whether the key is in the map.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table2_5_3: Whether the key is there, and its value through out.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table2_6_3: Takes the pair away, and tells whether the key was there.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.table2_7_3: Every key, or every value, in a List.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.text1: An array holds a fixed number of values of one type, numbered from 0. You make one with new and its length: new int[4] makes an array of four ints, with the indexes 0 to 3. Length tells how many places the array has. An index outside the array stops the program with a message, as the [runtime stops page](jsc:sigma_runtime_stops) explains. Arrays are in Sigma and in Sigma#.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.text2: A List is a growable row of values of one type, written List<int> for a list of ints. You make one with new List<int>(), and each Add puts one more item at the end. Sigma# only.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.text3: A Map holds pairs: a key, and the value that belongs to it. Map<string, int> makes a map from text keys to int values. Put adds a pair, and the key finds the value again. A map has no Clear member. Sigma# only.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.text4: To find out whether a key is there before you read it, use ContainsKey, or use TryGet, which tells you and gives the value back through out in one call. A map is indexed with the key in brackets, as in count["apple"].
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.text5: A foreach statement walks a List or an array, one item after another. A map cannot be walked with foreach: walk its Keys() or its Values() instead, which are Lists.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.text6: Sigma refuses the List and Map types and any type written with angle brackets. In Sigma, use an array with a count of your own beside it, or use two arrays for pairs.
jsc.guide.sigma_list_map.title: Lists and maps
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.definitio: A name written in front of a line of a method, which a jump can point to.
A line that starts with a dot, such as .arch, .field or .method, and names a part of the program.
The thing written after an instruction's name, such as a number or a name.
One numbered slot in a method, where it keeps one value while it runs.
The line that says how many places a method has.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.fix1: A listing edited by hand can lose its version line. Compile the source again.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.fix2: The listing needs a runtime that reads its version. Use a runtime that does.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.fix3: Compile the source again with the current compiler.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.fix4: Build the program for this machine's instruction set, or run it on a machine that runs it.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.problem1: The machine shows an A4001 problem, a missing version line.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.problem2: The machine shows an A4002 problem, a listing newer than the runtime reads.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.problem3: The machine shows an A4012 problem, a listing older than the runtime reads.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.problem4: The machine shows an A4015 problem, which says the program was built for another instruction set.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1: Problems in the text of the listing
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_10: nothing in this method is labelled '<name>'
A jump points to a label that the method does not have. Check the spelling, or add the label.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_11: this listing is assembly version <version> and this runtime reads version <version> and later: compile its source again
The listing is older than the runtime reads. Compile the source again with the current compiler.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_12: this method has no slots line, so it has no body
The method does not say how many places it has. Compile the source again.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_13: place <place> does not exist: this method has <count>
An instruction uses a place the method does not have. Use a place inside the count the message gives.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_14: '<name>' labels more than one line of this method
Two lines of one method have the same label. Keep one label for each line.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_1_: the listing has to begin with a version line
The first line is not a version line. Compile the source again.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_2_: this runtime reads assembly version <version>, and this listing is version <version>
The listing came from a newer compiler than this runtime reads, so it needs a runtime that reads its version.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_3_: The name is not an instruction of the listing format. Check the spelling, or compile the source again.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_4_: An instruction needs an operand and has none. Write the operand, or compile the source again.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_5_: An instruction has an operand it does not take. Remove the operand.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_6_: The operand is the wrong kind of value for that instruction or directive.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_7_: '<name>' is not a line this format has
A line starts with a dot and names no line the format has. Check the spelling.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_8_: an instruction has to be inside a method
An instruction line stands outside any method. Put it inside a method.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_9_: '<name>' has to be inside a type
A directive stands outside any type. Put it inside a type.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table1_he: What it means and the fix
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table2: Problems with the program and the machine
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table2_1_: A call, a new object or a field names something the machine does not have. Check the spelling of the name.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table2_2_: '<name>' can be read but not written
The program writes to a property that can only be read. Read its value, and do not write to it.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table2_3_: built for <instruction set>; this machine is <instruction set>
The program was built for another instruction set than this machine runs, so build it for this machine's instruction set or run it on a machine that runs that set.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.table2_he: What it means and the fix
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.text1: A listing is the text file the compiler writes for a program. The machine reads the listing when the program starts, and a listing problem is a line it cannot read. A listing problem stops the program from starting, and the machine shows you the first problem only.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.text2: The machine shows the program's name, a colon, and then the problem line. For example: "<program>: (4,1): error A4003: 'nonsense' is not an instruction". A listing problem always shows column 1.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.text3: Listing problems come from three causes: a listing you edited by hand, a listing made by another compiler version, and a machine that does not run the instruction set the program was built for. A listing that the editor builds cleanly shows no listing problem.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.text4: The runtime reads listing versions 2 and 3. A listing with no version line gives A4001, and the reader stops there. A version line with no number is read as the newest version. After a version problem, the reader reads no further, so that one problem is the only one shown.
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.text5: The problem with A4015 is different. The listing is fine, and the machine is the wrong one. The names that A4013 refers to are the ones described in [the library](jsc:sigma_library).
jsc.guide.sigma_listing_errors.title: Listing errors
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.definiti: Written on a method or a field, it means the member belongs to the class, not to one object.
A name in the header of a method, which receives the value passed to it.
A value you pass to a method when you call it.
One of several methods with the same name, told apart by their parameters.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.fix1: Check the number of values in the call against the parameters in the header.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.fix2: Give the arguments exact types, so that only one overload fits.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.fix3: Write out in front of the variable in the call.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.fix4: Set the out parameter before each return, as Split does before it returns.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.fix5: Declare the variable with exactly the type of the parameter.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.fix6: Write out instead, so the method fills in a value that the caller then reads.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.problem1: The compiler says no version of 'Twice' takes those arguments.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.problem2: The compiler says the call to 'Twice' fits more than one version of it.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.problem3: The compiler says 'half' is filled in by the method, so the argument is written with out.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.problem4: The compiler says 'half' is filled in by this method, so it must be given a value before every way out.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.problem5: The compiler says an out argument is exactly 'int', with no conversion on the way.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.problem6: The compiler says 'ref' is written only for strcat.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.table1_1: A static method that gives back an int, from one parameter.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.table1_2: A method that gives back nothing.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.table1_3: A method with an out parameter, which the method fills in.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.text1: A method is a named piece of code that you call by name, often with values to work on. Its header says what the method gives back, its name and its parameters. Its body holds the statements that run. A method that gives nothing back has void as its result type.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.text2: A static method belongs to the class itself. You call it through the name of the class, as Maths.Twice(4). A method without static belongs to one object, and you call it on that object, as till.Show("hi").
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.text3: The values you pass to a method are its arguments. The method receives them in its parameters, which are the names in its header. A value type argument is copied, so the method cannot change the caller's variable. An object is passed as the same object, so the method can change what the caller sees.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.text4: Several methods can share one name when their parameters differ. These are overloads. The compiler picks the version whose parameters fit the arguments. A call that fits no version is refused, and so is a call that fits two versions equally well.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.text5: An out parameter lets a method give a second value back. The header writes out in front of the parameter, and the method must fill it in before every way out. The caller writes out in front of an existing variable of exactly the parameter's type.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.text6: The keyword ref is written only for strcat, which joins text onto the text that a variable holds. A method that needs to fill in a value uses out instead. A method may also call itself: each call takes room on the stack of calls, and a chain more than 1,024 calls deep stops the program, as the [runtime stops](jsc:sigma_runtime_stops) page explains.
jsc.guide.sigma_methods_out_ref.title: Methods, out and ref
jsc.guide.sigma_namespaces_using.fix1: Add that using line at the top of the file.
jsc.guide.sigma_namespaces_using.fix2: Write 'using System.IO.*;' to bring in everything in it, or name one of its types.
jsc.guide.sigma_namespaces_using.fix3: Move the using line above the namespace line.
jsc.guide.sigma_namespaces_using.fix4: Write using Standard.*; instead, which holds everything that Sigma has.
jsc.guide.sigma_namespaces_using.problem: The compiler says 'Console' is in System.IO; add 'using System.IO.*;' or 'using System.IO.Console;' at the top of the file.
The compiler says 'System.IO' names a namespace.
The compiler says a using has to come before the namespace and the types.
The compiler refuses using System in Sigma.
jsc.guide.sigma_namespaces_using.table1_: The library of Sigma, which Sigma# also has: Console, File, Math, Script and more.
Other parts of the library. The [library chapter](jsc:sigma_library) describes them.
jsc.guide.sigma_namespaces_using.table2: The start of a new project
jsc.guide.sigma_namespaces_using.text1: Every type of a program belongs to a namespace, which is a name that groups types. A file declares its namespace with one line before its types, such as namespace Shop;. Every type in the file then belongs to that namespace, so two programs can each have a type called Till without a clash. When you write a program, the first lines tell the compiler where the types it uses come from.
jsc.guide.sigma_namespaces_using.text2: The library is grouped into namespaces as well. A program that wants a library type writes a using line at the top of the file, before the namespace line. using System.IO.*; brings in everything in System.IO, and using System.IO.Console; brings in one type only.
jsc.guide.sigma_namespaces_using.text3: A using line for a whole namespace is written with a star, such as using System.IO.*;. A line that names one type has no star. A program written in Sigma writes using Standard.*; to reach the library of Sigma.
jsc.guide.sigma_namespaces_using.text4: A type that the program declares itself wins over a library type with the same name. A full name, such as System.IO.Console.PrintLine("hi"), works in Sigma# without a using line, and Sigma refuses full names.
jsc.guide.sigma_namespaces_using.title: Namespaces and using
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.definition: A signal that a step failed, which a program can catch and handle somewhere else.
A library call that gives back true or false for success, and writes its result through out.
A failure of the machine itself on one instruction, which stops only that program.
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.fix1: Check that the name holds an object before you use it, for example by creating the object with new first.
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.fix2: Do not use an object after you dispose of it. See [Freeing objects with dispose](jsc:sigma_dispose).
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.fix3: Check that the divisor is not zero before you divide.
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.fix4: Neither language has try: check the value before the step, or use a Try form in Sigma#.

jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.problem2: The program stops and says this was disposed and cannot be used.
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.problem3: The program stops and says divided by zero.

jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.table1_6_2: A bool: whether the key is there, and its value through out

jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.table2_2_1: took the remainder of a division by zero
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.table2_2_2: A remainder with a divisor of zero.

jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.table2_3_2: A name that holds nothing is used as if it held an object.
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.table2_4_1: there is no place 4 in an array of 4
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.table2_4_2: An index that is outside the array.
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.table2_5_1: this was disposed and cannot be used

jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.table2_6_2: The program asks for more memory than it may use.
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.text1: Many languages report a failed step with an exception, which another part of the program can catch and handle. This language has no exceptions. It has no try, catch, throw or finally, and the compiler refuses those words as the start of a statement. When you read a number from text in Sigma#, use a Try form first, so the program does not stop.
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.text2: Instead, a program can ask first with a Try form, or it can let the problem stop it. A Try form is a library call that says whether it worked, and gives its result back through out. Sigma's own Convert and File offer fewer calls, and the Try forms are not among them. The [numbers page](jsc:numbers_and_time) and the [files page](jsc:files_and_file_handles) show what Sigma offers.
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.text3: A halt is different. The program stops at once, writes a message to its console, and does not go on. Nothing catches a halt. The full list of messages is in the [runtime stops page](jsc:sigma_runtime_stops).
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.text4: A fault is different again. The machine itself failed on one instruction, and only that one program stops. The message says that the runtime could not carry the step out.
jsc.guide.sigma_no_exceptions.title: No exceptions: Try forms and halts
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.definition1: A piece of code that gives back a value, such as 2 + 3 or a name.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.definition2: A symbol that combines values, such as + or ==.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.definition3: The rule that decides which operator is worked out first when a line has several.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.fix1: Compare texts with string.Compare, which gives a number to put in order.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.fix2: An if, a while or a for needs a true or false test. Write if (count > 0) instead of if (count).
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.fix3: Store the value in a variable, or pass it to a method, so the line does something.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.fix4: Put a name on the left of the equals sign, such as total = 5;
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.problem1: The compiler says '<' cannot be applied to 'string' and 'string'.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.problem2: The compiler says "a condition is a bool, not 'int'".
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.problem3: The compiler says "only a call, an assignment, an increment, a decrement or a new object can be used as a statement".
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.problem4: The compiler says "the left side of an assignment must be a variable, a field, a property or an element".
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.table1_14_1: Member, call, index and after a value
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.table2_2_2: Whether both are true, or both are false.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.table2_5_2: Whether both names point to the same object, not what it holds.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.table3_5_2: Numbers only, before or after the name.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.text1: An operator is a symbol that combines values: + adds two numbers, and == asks whether two values are equal. A piece of code that gives back a value, such as 2 + 3 or a name, is an expression. You join expressions with operators to make bigger expressions.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.text2: When one line has several operators, precedence decides which one is worked out first. Multiplication binds tighter than addition, so 2 + 3 * 4 is 14, not 20. Parentheses override the order: (2 + 3) * 4 is 20.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.text3: The arithmetic operators are + for adding, - for subtracting, * for multiplying, / for dividing and % for the remainder. When both sides of / are whole numbers, the result is a whole number: the fraction is cut off, so 7 / 2 is 3, and 7 % 2 is 1. Dividing by zero, or taking a remainder with zero, stops the program with a message.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.text4: The + operator joins text. When one side is text, the result is text, so "y = " + y puts the number after the words. The comparison operators < <= > >= work on numbers only. To put two texts in order, use string.Compare, as the text page explains.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.text5: The ++ operator adds one, and -- takes one away. A line can hold only the operator, such as count++ on its own. Inside a bigger expression, the form after the name gives the old value, and the form before the name gives the new one.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.text6: The compound forms join an operator to an assignment. total += 5; does the same as total = total + 5;, and the same goes for the other compound forms.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.text7: A shift moves the bits of the number on its left by the count on its right, and gives a number of the kind on its left. It takes only the low bits of the count, as C# does: five for an int and six for a long. So 1 << 32 is 1, and 1 << 33 is 2.
jsc.guide.sigma_operators.title: Operators and their order
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.definit: One program packed into a single text file, with its manifest and every file it carries.
The package.cpk text file that describes a package: its name, version, entry and files.
The compiled .asm file that the compiler writes from a source file.
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.fix1: Write the name in lower case, with only letters, digits and dashes, such as my-shop.
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.fix2: Write three numbers with dots, such as 1.0.0.
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.fix3: Write the file name of the listing on the entry line, such as shop.asm.
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.fix4: Compile the source with the compiler ([](jsc:sigma_compile)), then name the .asm file it writes.
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.fix5: Add a file line with the same name as the entry.
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.fix6: Pick one of the eight icons: gear, chart, box, bell, wrench, flask, eye or clock.
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.fix7: Write 1 or a larger whole number on the ram line.
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.fix8: Add a file line for each file the package carries.

jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.problem: The build says package.cpk: name: must be lowercase letters, digits or dashes; got "My Shop".

The build says package.cpk: entry: name the listing the package runs.
The build says package.cpk: entry: must be a compiled listing; got "shop.sgs".

The build says package.cpk: icon: must be one of gear, chart, box, bell, wrench, flask, eye, clock; got "star".
The build says package.cpk: ram: a package needs at least a megabyte to run in.
The build says package.cpk: files: a package with no files in it is not a package.

jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.step2: Edit package.cpk and change the lines you need.
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.table1_: The package's name: lower case letters, digits and dashes, at most 32 characters.
Three numbers with dots between them, such as 1.0.0. Each number has 1 to 4 digits.
The software house the Mirror lists beside the package.
The listing the package runs. It ends in .asm and must also be named on a file line.

jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.table2_: The name you typed, in lower case, or program.
