jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.text1: A package is one program packed up for somebody else. It holds the program's files and a short description of them, called the manifest. You can write a manifest by hand, and the game reads it the same way whoever wrote it.
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.text2: The manifest is a plain text file named package.cpk. It has one thing on each line: a key, a colon, then the value, such as name: shop. The game reads the keys without regard to capitals. It skips a line with no colon, and any line that starts with a hash sign (#).
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.text3: A key the game does not know is passed over, not refused. So a manifest written for a later version is still read here, without the newer ideas. When you publish a package, it goes to [the Mirror](jsc:mirror), the package service of the network, and the game checks the manifest first. The ram line is only recorded: the game does not refuse a package on a small computer.
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.text4: The icon is one of eight pictures the game already has: gear, chart, box, bell, wrench, flask, eye and clock. A package cannot bring its own artwork.
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.text5: In the folder you work in, type sgpack init and a name. The game makes the name lower case. If you type no name, the package is called program. The command writes package.cpk into that folder.
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.text6: The command refuses to write over a manifest that is already there. It answers "package.cpk is already here; edit it, or delete it to start over".
jsc.guide.sigma_package_manifest.title: What a package says about itself
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.definit: The text that printf prints, with holes in it where values go.
A place in a format string, marked with a percent sign and a letter, where a value is written.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.fix1: Write the format string directly in the call, between double quotes.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.fix2: Give one value for each hole, in the same order.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.fix3: Use %s for text, or give a whole number to the hole.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.fix4: Use one of the holes in the table above.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.fix5: Use a project that is held to version 2, or use printf, which every version has.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.problem: The compiler says printf's format has to be written out where it is used, in quotes, so its holes can be read.
The compiler says printf: the format has 2 holes and the call gives 1 value.
The compiler says printf: '%d' takes a whole number, and this is text.
The compiler says '%q' is no hole printf has.
The compiler says 'strlen' needs version 2; this project is version 1.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.table1: The holes of a format string
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.table1_: Flags such as - and 0, and a width or precision up to 999
A whole number, an int or a long
Nothing: it writes a percent sign
Nothing: it is accepted and means nothing
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.table2: Some old names and their long way
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.text1: Sigma keeps a set of short names from an older style of programming, such as printf, strlen and puts. You call them with no type in front, and they work in Sigma and in Sigma#. The one you meet first is printf, which prints a text with values in it.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.text2: printf takes a format string and then one value for each hole. It prints the text to the console and gives nothing back. The format string must be written in the call itself, in quotes, so that the compiler can check its holes against the values.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.text3: This program prints n = 42, text = ok. The first hole takes the whole number n, and the second takes the text ok.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.text4: The number of holes must match the number of values. Each hole also wants a kind of value: %d wants a whole number, %s wants text, and %c wants a char. The compiler checks all of this before the program runs.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.text5: sprintf takes the same format and values, and gives back the text instead of printing it. scanf reads one value from the console into a variable. Its format has exactly one hole and nothing else, and the variable is written with out, as in scanf("%d", out n). It gives back 1 when it read a value, and 0 when what was typed was not one. Every old name except printf needs version 2 of the project.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.text6: Each old name is one call of the library, and it gives the same value as the long way. strlen(text) gives the same as text.Length. A method or a variable of your own with the same name wins over the old name.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.text7: The [old names in the library](jsc:standard_functions) page lists every old name and the call it makes.
jsc.guide.sigma_printf_old_names.title: printf and the old names
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.definition1: The language version a project is held to. Version 1 is the first language, and version 2 is the current one.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.definition2: The version a build really uses: the lower of the project's langversion and the version of the installed compiler.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.fix1: Set the project's Language version to Default, or to version 2.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.fix2: Update the compiler package, or use a lower version after --lang.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.problem1: "'puts' needs Σ# 2; this project is Σ# 1" appears.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.problem2: "this compiler knows Σ# 1 at most; Σ# 2 needs a newer one" appears.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.problem3: "'3' is not a version of Σ#; there are 1 to 2" appears.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.step1: Open the Properties popup of the project in Virtual Studio.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.step3: Press the Default button to follow the installed compiler, or press a numbered button to hold the project to that version.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.table1_2_2: One of console, script, library or empty.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.table1_3_2: jsc:sigma for Sigma, or jsc:sigma_sharp for Sigma#.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.table1_4_2: One line for each source file, relative to the project folder.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.table1_5_2: One line for each library project it uses.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.table1_6_2: The listing it builds, such as build/NAME.asm. Empty for a library.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.table1_7_2: The instruction set it builds for, such as jsc:x86.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.table1_8_2: The language version it is held to. Written only when set. Without it, the project follows the installed compiler.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.text1: A project keeps the files of one program together, with the settings that build it. When you make a project, its settings live in the project file, a text file in the project folder. The file of Sigma# is named NAME.sgsproj, and the file of Sigma is named NAME.sgproj.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.text10: Version 1 is the first release. Version 2 added the types for the network, the machines and the windows, such as Bus, CraftInterface, Table and Chart. It added members to older types, such as Console.Read and File.Move. It also lets Main return an int and take the arguments, and the smaller Sigma gained Random.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.text2: Each line of the file holds one setting, as a key, a colon and a value. A line written in another way is skipped.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.text3: The kind tells the compiler what to build. A console program runs and returns. A script stays up. A library holds shared classes and has no start of its own. An empty project has nothing in it yet.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.text4: A solution keeps its projects together, one folder for each project. Its file lists each project by its path, and it names the startup project, the one that Start runs. When the startup project is empty, Start uses the first project that can run.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.text5: A project builds for one instruction set, which you choose in the popup named Platform target.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.text6: Sigma and Sigma# share their version numbers. Sigma 2 is the subset of Sigma# 2, so a project has a single number for both.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.text7: Under the buttons, Virtual Studio explains the choice. "Default follows the installed compiler (sgsc 2.0)." is the first hint. "A lower version refuses what came after it:" is the second. After you choose a number, the popup says "Written to the project as langversion" with that number.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.text8: Choosing Default removes the langversion line from the project file. Your build then uses the installed compiler's version. With a number, your build uses the lower of that number and the installed compiler's version.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.text9: On the command line the project file is not read. The option --lang sets the version for one compile ([](jsc:sigma_compile)). The sigma run command on a source file uses the newest version, not the project's.
jsc.guide.sigma_projects.title: Projects and versions
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.fix1: Connect this computer to a network whose Mainframe runs the Mirror, and switch that Mainframe on ([](jsc:mirror)).
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.fix2: Run sgpack build first, then publish the .cpk file it makes.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.fix3: Take a package you no longer need off the Mirror ([](jsc:sigma_unpublish)).
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.fix4: Name the file, such as sgpack publish mypkg-1.0.0.cpk, or run the command in the folder that holds the manifest.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.problem1: Publish says could not resolve mirror:// - connect this computer to a network whose Mainframe runs the Mirror service.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.problem2: Publish says mypkg-1.0.0.cpk: this is not a package (build one with 'sgpack build').
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.problem3: A new name is refused: the Mirror is full (64 packages).
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.problem4: Publish says name the package to publish, or run this beside a package.cpk.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.step1: Build the package, so that its .cpk file is in the folder.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.step2: Type sgpack publish and press [[Enter]]. The command publishes the package the manifest describes.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.step3: To publish another file, type sgpack publish and its file name, such as mypkg-1.0.0.cpk.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.table1_1_: Writes a package.cpk to fill in.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.table1_2_: Makes the package the manifest describes.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.table1_3_: Puts it on the network's Mirror.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.table1_4_: Takes it back off the Mirror.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.text1: Publishing puts a built package on [the Mirror](jsc:mirror), the package service that lives on the network's Mainframe ([](jsc:mainframes)). Once it is there, any computer on the network can install it by name.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.text2: The Mirror serves packages only when it is installed on the Mainframe and the Mainframe is running. A Mainframe that is switched off keeps the Mirror installed, but serves nothing until it is on again.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.text3: A successful publish answers published mypkg 1.0.0 on the Mirror, with the name and the version. Publishing a name that is already there answers replaced mypkg 1.0.0 on the Mirror, and the new copy takes the old one's place in a single step.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.text4: The Mirror holds up to 64 packages per network. A new name is refused at that count. Replacing a name you already published does not count against the limit.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.text5: The Mirror keeps the whole text of each package, and it does not record who published it. A successful publish also earns the achievement Ship It ([](jsc:achievements_sigma)), which asks you to pack a program with sgpack and publish it to the Mirror.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.text6: Publish checks the package before it sends it. It names only the first problem it finds, so fix that line and publish again.
jsc.guide.sigma_publish_mirror.title: Publishing a package to the Mirror
jsc.guide.sigma_reading_an_error.definit: Turning the source text of a program into a listing that a machine can run.
The text file the compiler writes from a program, with the steps the machine runs. Its file name ends in asm.
jsc.guide.sigma_reading_an_error.fix1: The file failed to compile, so it has no listing to run. Open it in the editor, fix its first problem and compile it again.
jsc.guide.sigma_reading_an_error.problem: The message says "Monitor.sgs does not compile" when you start the program.
jsc.guide.sigma_reading_an_error.table1_: The source file that holds the mistake, under the name you saved it.
The line and the column, both counted from 1 at the top left of the file.
The kind of line. Every line the compiler gives you is an error.
The error code. It names the kind of mistake, and it is the same in every language.
What the mistake is, in words, with the names it found in it.
jsc.guide.sigma_reading_an_error.text1: When you compile a Sigma program, the compiler checks every file of the program and lists each mistake it finds. A compile is one run of the compiler over your files, and the result is either a listing the machine can run or a list of mistakes. Each mistake takes one line, and that line tells you where it is, what kind it is and what it is about.
jsc.guide.sigma_reading_an_error.text2: For example, a mistake in a file called Monitor.sgs can read like this: "Monitor.sgs(12,9): error S2001: expected ';' but found '}'". The compiler expected a semicolon at line 12, column 9, and found a closing brace instead.
jsc.guide.sigma_reading_an_error.text3: A mistake in a listing has the same shape, but no file name: "(4,1): error A4003: 'nonsense' is not an instruction". Read it the same way. The listing errors have their own page: [listing errors](jsc:sigma_listing_errors).
jsc.guide.sigma_reading_an_error.text4: Read the list from the top and fix the first line first. A mistake early in a file can cause the lines after it, so the rest of the list can change when you fix it. The list is sorted by file, then by line, then by column.
jsc.guide.sigma_reading_an_error.text5: The compiler lists at most 100 mistakes for each file. When a file has more, the last line of the list reads "too many errors; the rest were not reported", and you fix the ones above it before you compile again.
jsc.guide.sigma_reading_an_error.text6: The editor's problem list, see [the editors](jsc:sigma_editors), groups the problems by file. The file with the most problems comes first, so the list starts with the file that needs the most work.
jsc.guide.sigma_reading_an_error.title: Reading an error line
jsc.guide.sigma_run.definition1: The memory a running program is given, measured in megabytes.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.fix1: Lower the --heap value, stop another program with sigma stop, or free memory on the computer.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.fix2: Build with scc, or run the listing on a Legacy computer or later.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.fix3: Compile the source file again, with the compiler that is installed.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.fix4: Run a file that ends in .asm, .sgs or .sg.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.fix5: Compile the source with sgsc or scc, and read the errors it names.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.problem1: "hello.asm: 16 MB will not fit in 8 MB of free memory" appears.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.problem2: "built for x86; this machine is IA-16" appears.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.problem3: A message names the listing's assembly version and the version this runtime reads.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.problem4: "hello.txt is not a Σ# program" appears.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.step1: Compile the source file, or have a listing ready.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.step2: Type sigma run hello.asm and press [[Enter]].
jsc.guide.sigma_run.step3: Type sigma ps to see the program in the list.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.step4: Type sigma stop 3 with the id from the list to stop it.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.table1_1_2: Starts a program. The word start does the same.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.table1_2_2: Stops a running program. The word kill does the same.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.table1_3_2: Lists the running programs. The word list does the same, and so does sigma alone.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.table2_1_2: A listing. The runtime starts it.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.table2_2_2: A source file. The runtime compiles it first, then runs it.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.table2_3_2: Refused: "hello.txt is not a Σ# program".
jsc.guide.sigma_run.table3_2_2: 64 MB. A larger request is cut to 64 MB, with no message.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.table4_1_2: The number that sigma stop takes.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.table4_2_2: The program's name, cut to 20 characters, with a ~ when it is cut.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.table4_3_2: running, parked (it waits for something outside it), finished, halted (it stopped on a mistake), or input (it waits for the keyboard).
jsc.guide.sigma_run.table4_4_2: The memory the program holds, out of the heap it was given, in KB (or in bytes when it is under 1,024).
jsc.guide.sigma_run.text1: A listing is ready to run, and the sigma command runs it. The runtime starts the program, keeps it in its list of running programs, and lets you stop it again.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.text2: When you run a source file, the runtime compiles it first. It uses the newest language version and the default instruction set of its language. The settings of a project do not apply to that compile.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.text3: Before a listing starts, the runtime makes three checks. It checks that the listing fits the computer's instruction set. It checks the listing's assembly version, which is refused when it is too old or too new. And it checks that the memory of the program fits in the free memory of the computer.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.text4: A running program gets its own memory, called the heap. The heap is measured in megabytes, and you set it with --heap.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.text5: A value that is not a number counts as zero, and zero gives the default. A --heap that is the last word is not a setting: it goes to the program as an argument.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.text6: Everything after the file, except --heap and its number, goes to the program. A Sigma program reads these words with Program.Args ([](jsc:programs_and_processes)). A Sigma# program can take them as a string array in Main, if its project is version 2.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.text7: With no program running, the list says so. Here is that answer:
jsc.guide.sigma_run.text8: Stopping a program answers stopped with its id, such as "stopped 3". An id that is not running answers "sigma: nothing is running as 3".
jsc.guide.sigma_run.text9: The full page of the sigma command follows.
jsc.guide.sigma_run.title: Running programs
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.definition: An error during a program's run, which stops the program at once and writes one message to its console.
One active method call on a thread. A thread keeps one frame for each call that has not returned yet.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.fix1: Check the number you divide by, before the division.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.fix10: This is not your program's fault. Report the line from the server log.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.fix2: Make the program hold fewer or smaller values, or give it more memory when it starts, up to 64 MB.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.fix3: Give the calling method an end, or use a loop instead.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.fix4: The text you convert is not a number, nor true or false. Check the input.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.fix5: Use a value inside the limit the message gives.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.fix6: The name is wrong for that kind of value. Use a member the value has.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.fix7: Join the computer to a network first.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.fix8: Take the lock before you let it go.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.fix9: Compile the source file first, so that a listing exists to run.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.problem10: It says the runtime could not carry this out.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.problem3: It says calls went deep, and a method may be calling itself without end.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.problem4: It says a text is not a number, or not true or false.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.problem5: It says a number, a place or a length is out of range, such as "a window holds at most 256 widgets".
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.problem6: It says there is no such member, or the runtime does not answer for a name.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.problem7: It says this computer is not on a network.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.problem8: It says this thread is letting go of a lock it does not hold.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.problem9: It says nothing installed runs a program of this kind.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_10_: The machine cannot start the program: no runner exists for that kind of file, there is not enough free memory, or the file cannot be read or started.
The message says why. Compile a source file first, free some memory on the machine, or check the file.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_11_: A value given to a component breaks a rule, or a computer is powered off.
The message gives the rule. Keep the value within it, and check the file or the computer.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_12_: A method calls itself without end, so the calls go too deep.
Give the recursion an end, or use a loop. The message names the method.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_13_: The runtime itself failed while it ran a step of the program.
This is not your program's fault. Report the line from the server log.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_1_2: A division or a remainder by zero, with whole numbers or with real numbers.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_1_3: Check the number you divide by before the division.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_2_2: A value is nothing where an object, a list, a map, an array, a thread or a process is needed.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_2_3: Make sure the value is set before you use it.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_3_2: An object was disposed and then used again.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_3_3: Do not use an object after it is disposed.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_4_2: The program holds more memory than it was given.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_4_3: Make it hold fewer or smaller values, or give it more memory when it starts, up to 64 MB.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_5_2: A conversion gets a text or a value of the wrong kind.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_5_3: Check the text you convert: a number conversion needs a number, and a true or false conversion needs true or false.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_6_2: A number, a place or a length is outside the range it may have.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_6_3: Use a value inside the limit the message gives.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_7_2: A name is wrong for that kind of value: the value has no such member.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_7_3: Use a member that the value has. The message names the value and the member.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_8_2: A program calls the network, but the computer is not on one.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_8_3: Join the computer to a network first.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_9_2: The thread lets go of a lock it does not hold.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.table1_9_3: Take the lock before you let it go.

jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.text1: A program can stop while it runs, when it meets an error it cannot go on from. This book calls that kind of stop a halt, and there are 13 of them. The program ends its run at once.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.text2: When a halt happens, the program's threads stop and the program lets go of its locks. The message is all you see of the stop. Most messages do not say which line of the program caused it.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.text3: The table below numbers the 13 stops, so you can find each one. The game shows you only the message, not the number. In this chapter a program's memory is counted in megabytes (MB).
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.text4: In the messages below, the words in angle brackets stand for the names and the numbers the game fills in.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.text5: Stops 10 and 11 can also show a message that the machine writes itself, for a bus, a crafting interface, a file or an [IQL](jsc:iql_getting_started) query. IQL, the Item Query Language, is the network's query language. Those messages come from the part of the machine that ran the step, so they are not in the table.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.text6: Stop 13 is the one that is not your program's fault. The runtime failed, and a line goes to the server log with the line of the program where it happened.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.text7: The stack places are counted as the frames times the places each frame uses. The memory you ask for is kept between 1 MB and 64 MB.
jsc.guide.sigma_runtime_stops.title: The stops while a program runs
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.definiti: A place inside a text where a value is put in: the braces of an interpolated string, or a marker of a printf format that the format fills with a value.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.fix1: The name is spelled wrong, or it is declared after this line. Check its spelling, or declare it above.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.fix2: Write the value as the type the message names, or change the type of the place it goes.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.fix3: Give the values the method takes, in the order it takes them.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.fix4: Keep exactly one class that implements IScript or has a static Main.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.problem1: It says '<name>' does not name anything here.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.problem3: It says no version of '<name>' takes those arguments.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.problem4: It says a program needs exactly one place to start.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table1_1: A name is newer than the language version your project holds to. Raise the project's version, or do not use the name.
This message is no longer shown, so you should not meet it. If you do, write the name of a type in that place.
'<name>' names a namespace; write 'using <name>.*;' to bring in everything in it, or name one of its types
A namespace was named where a type is needed. Write the using line with a star, or name one type of the namespace.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table1_2: The name is not declared where you use it. Check its spelling, or declare it above this line.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table1_3: Two things have the same name in one place. Give one of them another name.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table1_4: '<name>' is in <namespace>; add 'using <namespace>.*;' or 'using <namespace>.<name>;' at the top of the file
The name lives in a namespace you did not bring in. Add the using line the message gives, at the top of the file.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table1_5: '<name>' already stands behind '<name>', so it cannot also stand in front of it
Two types each name the other as their base, in a circle. Remove the base that closes the circle.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table1_6: '<name>' is <private or protected> to '<type>', so it cannot be reached from here
The member is private to its type, which is what a member written with no word of access is, or protected to it and the types that stand on it. Mark it public, or reach it from inside its type.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table1_7: only a class or an interface can stand behind the colon, and '<name>' is neither
A type takes a base after its colon that is not a class or an interface. Name a class or an interface there.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table1_8: a struct can implement interfaces but stands on no class, and '<name>' is a class
A struct names a class as its base, but a struct can only implement interfaces. Remove the class, or make the type a class.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table1_9: The program uses a base-class member where its type has no base class. Check the type, or remove that use.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table1_h: What it means and the fix
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table2_1: A value of one type is used where another type is needed, with no safe conversion. Write a value of the right type.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table2_2: A generic type got the wrong number of types. Give it the count the message says.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table2_3: an enum's number has to be written as a number
An enum value gives a number that is not written as a plain number. Write the number itself.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table2_4: a condition is a bool, not '<type>'
An if or a loop tests something that is not true or false. Write a test that gives true or false.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table2_5: only an object can be disposed, not '<type>'
Dispose works on objects only. Dispose an object, not a plain value.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table2_6: only an object can be locked, not '<type>'
Lock works on objects only. Lock an object.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table2_7: foreach walks an array or a list, not '<type>'
A foreach loop needs an array or a list. Give it one of them.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table2_h: What it means and the fix
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table3_1: '<member>' belongs to the type, not to one of its objects
Write the type's name before the dot, not the name of one of its objects.
'<member>' belongs to an object, not to the type
A member of an object is used through the type's name. Use an object of the type.
'<name>' is not available in a static member
A static member has no object, so this value does not exist there. Use a value that does not need an object.
'<name>' is a method: call it, or hand it over where a delegate of its shape is wanted
A method is used as a value without its brackets. Call it, or give it where a delegate is expected.
this lambda does not have the shape '<shape>' takes
The lambda's values do not match the delegate it is given to. Make it take the values the delegate takes.
The two values do not work together with this operator. Use values of a type the operator takes.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table3_2: The operator does not take this type. Use a value of a type it takes.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table3_3: The index is the wrong kind of value for this type. Give an index of the kind it takes.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table3_4: '<name>' is not something that can be called
You called a name that is not a method or a delegate. Check the spelling, or call a method.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table3_5: new was used with a type that cannot be made that way. Make an object of a type that can.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table3_6: '<type>' is abstract, so it cannot be made with new
An abstract type has no objects of its own. Make an object of a type that is not abstract.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table3_7: no version of '<name>' takes those arguments
The values you give fit no version of the method. Give values of the types one version takes.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table3_8: the call to '<name>' fits more than one version of it
More than one version fits the values. Give a value of a type that fits only one version.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table3_9: The name is not a member of that type. Check the spelling, or use a member the type has.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table3_h: What it means and the fix
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table4_1: this switch already has that label
Two cases of the switch have the same label. Keep one of them.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table4_2: 'break' only means something inside a loop or a switch
break stands outside any loop or switch. Move it inside one, or delete it.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table4_3: 'continue' only means something inside a loop
continue stands outside any loop. Move it inside a loop, or delete it.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table4_4: a method that gives back '<type>' must return a value
The method ends without giving back a value. Return a value of that type.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table4_5: a method that gives back nothing cannot return a value
The method returns a value, but it gives back nothing. Remove the value after return.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table4_h: What it means and the fix
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table5_1: '<name>' is filled in by the method, so the argument is written with out
The method fills in this argument. Write out before it.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table5_2: '<name>' is read by the method, so the argument cannot be written with out
The method only reads this argument. Remove out.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table5_3: an out argument is exactly '<type>', with no conversion on the way
The out variable must be exactly the type the method fills. Declare it with that type.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table5_4: '<name>' is filled in by this method, so it must be given a value before every way out
One way out of the method leaves the out value empty. Give it a value before every return.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table5_5: '<name>' is not somewhere a method can write
The method can only write into a place. Give it a place, not a plain value.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table5_6: an event can only be raised inside the type that declares it
The event is raised from outside its type. Raise it inside the type.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table5_7: an event's type must be a delegate, and '<type>' is not one
An event needs a delegate type. Give it a delegate.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table5_8: 'ref' is written only for strcat, which joins onto the text '<name>' holds; a method fills in with out
ref is only for joining text. Use out for a method that fills a value in.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table5_h: What it means and the fix
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table6_1: The modifier does not fit this kind of member. Remove it.
'<name>' is readonly, so it can only be written where it is declared or in a constructor
A readonly value is written only where it is declared or in a constructor. Move the write there.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table6_2: '<method>' is already on '<type>', so write it with override to replace it
The method replaces one from a base type. Write override before it.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table6_3: '<method>' on '<type>' is not virtual, so nothing can replace it; mark it virtual there
The base method cannot be replaced. Mark it virtual in its own type.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table6_4: '<method>' is written with override but nothing above '<type>' has it
override names a method that no base type has. Remove override, or check the name.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table6_5: '<method>' has no body, so '<type>' has to be declared abstract
A method without a body makes its type abstract. Declare the type abstract.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table6_6: '<method>' is abstract, so it is written with a semicolon and no body
An abstract method ends with a semicolon and has no body. Remove the body.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table6_7: '<method>' has no body, so it is written with abstract
A method without a body must be abstract. Write abstract before it.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table6_8: '<type>' is not abstract, so it has to give '<method>' a body
A type that is not abstract must give a body to each abstract member it has. Give the method a body.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table6_9: '<type>' says it is a '<kind>' but does not have '<member>'
The type says it implements something but misses one of its members. Write the missing member.

jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table7: The entry point and the subset
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table7_1: a program needs exactly one place to start, either a class that implements IScript or a class with a static Main, and this one has <count>
The program has no place to start, or more than one. Keep exactly one class that implements IScript or has a static Main.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table7_2: A Sigma file uses a feature only Sigma# has. Write the file in Sigma#, or use the alternative the message names.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table7_h: What it means and the fix
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table8_1: <name>'s format has to be written out where it is used, in quotes, so its holes can be read
A printf format is kept in a name. Write the format as text in quotes, where it is used.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table8_2: The format text is wrong. The second part of the message says what is wrong with it.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table8_3: <name>: the format has <count> and the call gives <count>
The format has a different number of holes than the call has values. Give one value for each hole.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table8_4: A hole takes one kind of value, and the call gives another. Give a value of the kind the hole takes.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.table8_h: What it means and the fix
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.text1: A meaning error is a line whose shape is right but whose names or types do not fit. The compiler checks meaning once the shape of the file is clean, so these codes usually appear after the syntax errors are gone. The editor's check while you type is the exception.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.text2: The words in angle brackets stand for what the compiler found in your file: a name, a type, a member of a type, a number or a token. Your message shows the real words in their place.
jsc.guide.sigma_semantic_errors.title: Meaning errors

jsc.guide.sigma_sharing_errors.table1_4_: A listed file is missing. Copy it into the folder, or remove its file line.

jsc.guide.sigma_sharing_errors.text1: Each error starts with a prefix that tells you where it came from. An sgpack error can start with sgpack:. A line that starts with package.cpk: points at a line of your manifest. A line that starts with a package file's name, such as mypkg-1.0.0.cpk:, comes from publish and points at that file.
jsc.guide.sigma_sharing_errors.text2: The table gives each text as the game shows it, with what it means and how to fix it.

jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.definition: The place of an item in a row, counted from 0, so the first item is at place 0.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.fix1: Use Substring to take a piece of the text instead.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.problem1: The compiler says 'string' cannot be indexed by 'int'.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.table1_10_: Puts two texts in order: below zero, zero or above zero.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.table1_1_3: How many characters the text holds. It is a property, so write no brackets.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.table1_2_3: The text from the place start to the end.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.table1_3_3: A piece of the text, of the length you give.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.table1_4_3: The place of the first match, counted from 0, or -1 when there is none.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.table1_5_3: Whether the text holds, starts with or ends with the piece you give.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.table1_6_3: A new text in capitals, in small letters, or without spaces at the ends.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.table1_7_3: A new text with every old piece changed to new.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.table1_8_2: A List of text, Sigma# only
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.table1_8_3: The pieces between the character you give.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.table1_9_3: Builds a text from a format and the values for its holes.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.text1: Text is a string: a row of characters between double quotes. A string is a reference type, so it can be null. A char is one character, written between single quotes, and inside the machine it is its number.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.text2: You join text with +. When one side is text, the result is text, so "n = " + 5 gives n = 5. Two texts are equal with == when they hold the same characters. Text cannot be compared with < or >: to put texts in order, use string.Compare, which needs version 2 of the project. It gives back a number below zero, zero or above zero.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.text3: Text cannot be indexed like an array: text[0] is refused. To take the first character as text, use Substring(0, 1).
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.text4: A char has its own tests: char.IsDigit(c), char.IsLetter(c), char.IsWhiteSpace(c), char.ToUpper(c) and char.ToLower(c). They need version 2 of the project. The older names, such as toupper, are on the [old names page](jsc:sigma_printf_old_names).
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.text5: A char in arithmetic becomes a number. 'A' + 1 is an int, not a character.
jsc.guide.sigma_strings_chars.title: Text and characters
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.definition: One piece of text that the compiler reads as a single unit: a word, a number, a string or a symbol.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.fix1: The line before the brace does not end with a semicolon. Add the semicolon at its end.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.fix2: The line holds a value that does nothing. Assign it, print it, or delete it.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.fix3: Write a namespace line at the top of the file, with a name you choose.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.fix4: Split the deep part into smaller parts. The rest of the file is not read until then.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.problem2: It says "only a call, an assignment, an increment, a decrement or a new object can be used as a statement".
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.problem3: It says every type is in a namespace.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.problem4: It says this is nested more than 128 levels deep.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table1_1_2: the string was never closed before the end of the line
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table1_1_3: A string has no closing quote on its line. Close it on the same line.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table1_2_2: the comment was never closed before the end of the file
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table1_2_3: A comment has no closing mark. Add the closing mark.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table1_3_2: '<character>' does not begin anything the language knows
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table1_3_3: The character is not part of the language. Remove it or replace it.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table1_4_2: '<text>' is not a number the language can read
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table1_4_3: A number has letters or a second dot stuck to it, or a value too big for its type. Write the number again.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table1_5_2: a character literal holds exactly one character
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table1_5_3: Two single quotes hold no character, or more than one. Keep exactly one character between them.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table1_6_2: '\<character>' is not an escape the language knows
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table1_6_3: A backslash is followed by a character that is not an escape. Use an escape the language has, or remove the backslash.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table1_hea: What it means and the fix
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_10_: a file declares one namespace on its own line, before its types; put more of them in blocks
The file has more than one namespace line. Keep one on its own line and write the others in blocks.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_11_: every type is in a namespace: put 'namespace Name;' at the top of the file
A type stands with no namespace. Write a namespace line at the top of the file.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_12_: this is nested more than 128 levels deep, which is more than the compiler reads; the rest of the file was not read
There are too many blocks inside blocks. Split the deep part into smaller parts.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_13_: '<word>' is kept for a later version of the language; for now, <alternative>

The file writes try, catch, finally, throw, goto or const. A later version of the language brings them, so they are kept already, and no name can be one of them. Until then, write what the message says: there are no exceptions, so a mistake halts the program and a call that can fail answers instead.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_1_3: The grammar needs one piece and finds another. Put the missing piece where the message says.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_2_3: A type name must stand here. Write the name of a type.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_3_3: A value must stand here, for example between the empty braces of an interpolated string. Write the value.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_4_2: expected a field, a method, a property or an event but found <token>
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_4_3: A line inside a type is none of these four. Write one of them, or remove the line.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_5_2: expected a class, a struct, a record, an interface, an enum or a delegate but found <token>
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_5_3: Where a type should start, the line starts with something else. Start the type with one of these words.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_6_2: only a call, an assignment, an increment, a decrement or a new object can be used as a statement
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_6_3: A line holds a value that does nothing, such as a + 1. Assign it, print it, or delete it.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_7_3: The same modifier stands twice, such as public public. Keep one of them.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_8_2: the left side of an assignment must be a variable, a field, a property or an element
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_8_3: The left side of the = sign must be a variable, a field, a property or an element. Put one of these there.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_9_2: a using has to come before the namespace and the types
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_9_3: A using line sits too low in the file. Move it above the namespace.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.table2_hea: What it means and the fix
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.text1: A syntax error is a mistake in the shape of the text. The compiler cannot read the line as a statement, a declaration or a value, because a piece is missing, extra or in the wrong place. The codes below are the mistakes you can see on the line they name.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.text2: The compiler cuts the text into tokens first. A token is one piece of text: a word, a number, a string or a symbol. A message shows a token in quotes, such as ';'. A token with no single spelling is shown by its kind: an integer, a long integer, a float, a double, a string, a character, a name, or the end of the file.
jsc.guide.sigma_syntax_errors.title: Syntax errors
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.definition: The smaller of the two programming languages. Its source files end in .sg, and its compiler is scc.
The full programming language, which accepts everything Sigma accepts. Its source files end in .sgs, and its compiler is sgsc.
A program that turns source text into a listing. When the source has an error, it prints the errors and writes nothing.
The assembly text a compiler writes, in a file that ends in .asm.
A text file that holds a program in Sigma or Sigma#, written before it is compiled.
A folder that holds the source files of one program, and the settings that build it.
The program that runs listings on a computer, and that gives the computer the sigma command.
The basic operations a processor knows. A listing is built for one set, and a computer runs it only if its processor knows that set.
The hardware generation of a computer. The era decides its instruction set and which software it can install.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.fix1: Write the program in Sigma, in a Sigma project. Or set its platform target to x86 or x86-64.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.fix2: The computer is a Vintage one, which runs only IA-16 listings. Build with scc, which builds for IA-16, or run the listing on a Legacy computer or later.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.problem1: The build stops with "IA-16 runs Σ only; write it in Σ, in a Σ project".
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.problem2: A listing is refused: "built for x86; this machine is IA-16".
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.table3: The instruction set of each era
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.table3_3_1: Transition, Standard, Advanced, Exa and Singularity
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.table4_10_: Two arrays, or one array searched for the key.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.table4_1_2: A class whose methods are virtual, and build on it instead.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.table4_2_2: A struct with the same fields.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.table4_3_2: A class with virtual methods that do nothing, and build on that.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.table4_4_2: Give it a body that does nothing, and write it virtual.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.table4_5_2: Call the method by name, or keep the object and call it through that.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.table4_6_2: Keep the object that wants telling, and call a method on it.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.table4_7_2: A field, or a method that gives the value back.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.table4_8_2: An array, or a class that holds exactly what you need.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.table4_9_2: An array, and a count of your own beside it.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.table4_hea: What the compiler suggests you write
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.text1: Sigma and Sigma# are the two programming languages of the computers here. They are one family: everything written in Sigma is also a valid Sigma# program. You learn one, and you can read the other.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.text10: Sigma has a smaller library than Sigma#. Its classes live in the namespace Standard, with Console, File, Math and Convert among them. The chapter [](jsc:sigma_library) lists what each one does.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.text2: Sigma keeps a [class](jsc:sigma_classes), a struct, an array, a loop and a call, and nothing else of the advanced kind. Sigma# adds what Sigma leaves out, such as threads, collections, interfaces and generics. A program written in Sigma compiles unchanged in Sigma#.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.text3: Which one should you choose? Your computer decides first. A Vintage computer can hold only the Sigma compiler, so Sigma is its only language. A Legacy computer or later holds the whole toolchain, and then Sigma# gives you the full library.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.text4: A compiler turns a source file into a listing: the assembly text that a computer runs, in a file that ends in .asm. Each listing is built for one instruction set.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.text5: The runtime runs the listings. It is a package of its own, and once it is installed it gives the computer the sigma command ([](jsc:sigma_installing)).
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.text6: Each computer runs one instruction set (ISA): the basic operations its processor knows. A listing is built for one set, and a computer runs it only if its processor knows that set. This mod has three: IA-16, x86 and x86-64.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.text7: A program built for the oldest instruction set keeps working on every newer one. That is why IA-16 listings run everywhere, and x86-64 listings run only on x86-64 machines.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.text8: Every computer also has an era, its hardware generation: Vintage, Legacy, Transition, Standard, Advanced, Exa or Singularity. The era decides which instruction set the computer has, and which software it can install. The eras are explained in [](jsc:eras).
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.text9: When you do not choose an instruction set, the build takes the oldest one the language runs on: IA-16 for Sigma, and x86 for Sigma#. So a Sigma# program built by default runs from a Legacy computer up, and never on a Vintage one.
jsc.guide.sigma_two_languages.title: Two languages, one family
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.definiti: A named blueprint for objects: it lists the fields and methods that each object has.
A value made from a class with new. It holds its own fields and runs its own methods.
A type whose values are objects that can be shared, so two names can point to one object.
A type whose values are copied whenever they are stored or handed over.
The empty value of a reference type, which points to no object.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.fix1: Use a cast if losing the fraction is what you want, or declare the variable as a double. The error is explained in [the meaning errors](jsc:sigma_semantic_errors).
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.fix2: Check the spelling, and check that you declared the variable above the line that uses it.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.fix3: Sigma has no var: write the type out, as in int x = 5;
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.problem1: The compiler says cannot convert 'double' to 'int'.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.problem2: The compiler says 'total' does not name anything here.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.table1_2: A whole number, in 64 bits, for bigger numbers.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.table1_3: A decimal number, shorter than a double.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.table1_4: A decimal number, with more precision.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.table1_6: One character. Inside the machine, its number.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.table1_7: Text, which is a reference type.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.text1: A variable is a named place that holds a value. Its type says what kind of value may go in it, and the compiler refuses anything else. You declare a variable by writing its type, then its name, and then, if you want, a first value.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.text2: Each declaration names exactly one variable. Write int total = 0; to declare one; a line such as int a, b; is refused.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.text3: Types fall into two groups, and the group decides what happens when you copy a value. A value type, such as int, bool or char, is copied whenever you store it or hand it over. A reference type, such as text or an object of a class, is shared: two names can point to the same object, so a change through one name shows through the other.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.text4: A text is a reference type, so it can hold null, the empty value.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.text5: Numbers go into bigger number types without asking. An int goes into a long, a float or a double. The other way needs a cast: you write the new type in brackets in front of the value, as in (int) 2.5. The cast tells the compiler that you accept the change. Without the cast, the line is refused.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.text6: The word null is the empty value of a reference type. It fits any type that holds objects, such as text or an object of a class, but it does not fit an int.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.text7: Sigma# has the word var, which reads the type from the value: var x = 5; makes x an int. Sigma refuses var, and you write the type out instead.
jsc.guide.sigma_types_variables.title: Types and variables
jsc.guide.sigma_unpublish.fix1: Type the package's name after unpublish.
jsc.guide.sigma_unpublish.fix2: The name is not on the Mirror. Check its spelling, then try again.
jsc.guide.sigma_unpublish.fix3: No Mirror serves this network. Connect to a network whose Mainframe runs the Mirror ([](jsc:mirror)).
jsc.guide.sigma_unpublish.problem1: The command says usage: sgpack unpublish <name>.
jsc.guide.sigma_unpublish.problem2: The command says the Mirror is not serving the name you typed.
jsc.guide.sigma_unpublish.problem3: The command says could not resolve mirror://.
jsc.guide.sigma_unpublish.step1: Type sgpack unpublish mypkg and press [[Enter]].
jsc.guide.sigma_unpublish.step2: Read the answer: took mypkg off the Mirror.
jsc.guide.sigma_unpublish.text1: Unpublishing removes a package from the Mirror, so no computer can install it after that. You name the package, not the file. The command is sgpack unpublish, followed by the package's name.
jsc.guide.sigma_unpublish.text2: Any player on the network can take any package off the Mirror. The Mirror keeps no record of who published a package, so nothing stops one player from removing another's package. Check with the other players before you take away a package they use.
jsc.guide.sigma_unpublish.title: Taking a package off the Mirror
jsc.guide.software_commands.definition1: A program that prints your system's logo beside a summary of the machine: its system, kernel, uptime, packages and shell.
jsc.guide.software_commands.fix1: The store command lists the programs you can install.
jsc.guide.software_commands.fix2: Put the disc in a drive joined to the computer, then run install again.
jsc.guide.software_commands.fix3: Connect the computer to a network whose [Mainframe](jsc:mainframes) runs the Mirror.
jsc.guide.software_commands.fix4: Run install screenfetch first, then type screenfetch again.
jsc.guide.software_commands.problem1: The install command says no such program.
jsc.guide.software_commands.problem2: The install command says the program needs its install disc in a linked drive.
jsc.guide.software_commands.problem3: A package command says it could not resolve mirror.
jsc.guide.software_commands.problem4: The shell says screenfetch: not found.
jsc.guide.software_commands.step1: Type store to list the programs you can install on this computer.
jsc.guide.software_commands.step2: Put the install disc of the program in a drive joined to the computer.
jsc.guide.software_commands.step3: Type install and the program's name, such as screenfetch.
jsc.guide.software_commands.step4: Type programs to see the installed programs, and check that yours is there.
jsc.guide.software_commands.table1_1_3: install, remove, search, list, update and upgrade
jsc.guide.software_commands.table1_3_3: -S to install, -R to remove, -Ss to search, -Q to list, -Syu to upgrade
jsc.guide.software_commands.table1_4_3: A name to install, --unmerge to remove, --search, --sync and --update @world
jsc.guide.software_commands.table1_5_3: install, delete, search, info, update and upgrade
jsc.guide.software_commands.table1_6_3: No package manager on this system
jsc.guide.software_commands.text1: There are two ways to add software to a Unix system, and this entry says which is which. The store installs a program from an install disc in a drive joined to the computer. A package manager installs and removes packages from the Mirror.
jsc.guide.software_commands.text2: A package manager works only on the system that uses it. Removing software on these systems is the package manager's job: there is no uninstall command here, because uninstall is a DOS command. If you are not sure how a command got here, type which, and it says whether the system or a package put it there.
jsc.guide.software_commands.text3: For the verbs of apt and dnf, read the Linux Desk Reference ([](jsc:apt)). For pkg, read the Daemon Handbook ([](jsc:pkg)). A package install or removal needs the Mirror, the network service that keeps the packages ([](jsc:mirror)).
jsc.guide.software_commands.text4: The screenfetch program prints a short summary of the system, with labels such as OS, Kernel, Uptime, Packages and Shell. You install it first, like any program of the store.
jsc.guide.software_commands.title: Installing and removing software
jsc.guide.software_verbs.definition1: The network's package service, which offers programs that you can install.
jsc.guide.software_verbs.definition2: A program that the Mirror offers, ready to fetch and set up.
jsc.guide.software_verbs.fix1: Type programs or store to see the ids, and check the spelling.
jsc.guide.software_verbs.fix2: Link a drive and put the disc in it ([](jsc:drives)).
jsc.guide.software_verbs.fix3: The computer is not on a network with a Mirror. Connect it to one ([](jsc:mirror)).
jsc.guide.software_verbs.fix4: Type search with no text to list the packages the Mirror offers.
jsc.guide.software_verbs.fix5: Type a package name after install or remove.
jsc.guide.software_verbs.fix6: Free some space on the disk, or use a larger disk.
jsc.guide.software_verbs.problem2: NAME needs its install disc in a linked drive
jsc.guide.software_verbs.problem3: could not resolve mirror:// - no package source reachable
jsc.guide.software_verbs.problem5: this verb needs a package name
jsc.guide.software_verbs.problem6: The installation could not be written to the disk (no space or no disk).
